title.zh: 卷一百二十七 志第八十 樂二
title.raw: 卷一百二十七 志第八十 樂二 Volume 127 Treatises 80: Music 2

sentences.zh: 景祐三年七月，馮元等上新修《景祐廣樂記》八十一卷，詔翰林學士丁度、知制誥胥偃、直史館高若訥、直集賢院韓琦取鄧保信、阮逸、胡瑗等鍾律，詳定得失可否以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of the Jingyou era, Feng Yuan and others presented the newly revised Records of Jingyou Broad Music in eighty-one volumes. An edict ordered Hanlin Academician Ding Du, drafter of imperial edicts Xu Yan, duty historian at Historiography Institute Gao Ruone, and duty scholar at Hall of Assembled Eminences Han Qi to take the pitch standards of Deng Baoxin, Ruan Yi, Hu Yuan, and others, examine in detail what was right or wrong and acceptable or not, and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jingyou 3, Feng Yuan and others submitted the newly revised Records of Jingyou Broad Music in eighty-one volumes. The throne ordered Hanlin Academician Ding Du, drafter of imperial edicts Xu Yan, duty historian at the Historiography Institute Gao Ruone, and duty scholar at the Hall of Assembled Eminences Han Qi to review the pitch standards of Deng Baoxin, Ruan Yi, Hu Yuan, and others, determine what was sound or flawed and what might be adopted, and report back.

sentences.zh: 九月，阮逸言：“臣等所造鍾磬皆稟於馮元、宋祁，其分方定律又出於胡瑗算術，而臣獨執《周禮》嘉量聲中黃鍾之法及《國語》鈞鍾弦準之製，皆抑而不用。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Ruan Yi said: "The bells and chime-stones that your subjects made were all directed by Feng Yuan and Song Qi; the method of assigning squares and fixing pitch laws further came from Hu Yuan's calculations. Yet I alone held to the method of the Jialiang sounding Huangzhong in the Rites of Zhou and the design of tuning bells and string standards in the Discourses of the States — all were suppressed and not used.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Ruan Yi memorialized: "The bells and chime-stones we made were all overseen by Feng Yuan and Song Qi, and the method of assigning squares and setting pitch laws came from Hu Yuan's mathematics. Yet I alone insisted on the Rites of Zhou method whereby the Jialiang sounds Huangzhong and on the Discourses of the States system of tuned bells and string pitch standards — and all of this was set aside and rejected.

sentences.zh: 臣前蒙召對，言王樸律高而李照鍾下。

translations.literal: Your subject was previously summoned for audience and said that Wang Pu's pitch standard was high while Li Zhao's bell tones were low.
translations.idiomatic: When I was previously summoned to audience, I stated that Wang Pu's pitch standard ran high while Li Zhao's bell tones ran low.

sentences.zh: 竊睹御製《樂髓新經曆代度量衡》篇，言《隋書》依《漢志》黍尺製管，或不容千二百，或不啻九寸之長，此則明班《志》已後，曆代無有符合者。

translations.literal: I have privately seen Your Majesty's own composition, the essay on measurements of successive dynasties in the Musical Essence New Classic, which states that the Book of Sui, following the millet-measure standard of the Han Treatise, made pipes that sometimes could not hold twelve hundred grains or sometimes exceeded nine inches in length — this shows clearly that after the Han Treatise, no generation had one that matched.
translations.idiomatic: I have read Your Majesty's own essay on successive dynasties' measures in the Musical Essence New Classic, which observes that the Book of Sui, following the Han Treatise's millet-measure standard in making pipes, sometimes could not hold twelve hundred grains and sometimes exceeded nine inches in length. This makes clear that since the Han Treatise, no later age has produced a standard that truly matched it.

sentences.zh: 惟蔡邕銅龠本得於《周禮》遺範，邕自知音，所以隻傳銅龠，積成嘉量，則是聲中黃鍾而律本定矣。

translations.literal: Only Cai Yong's bronze yue tube was originally obtained from the surviving model of the Rites of Zhou. Yong himself understood pitch; therefore he transmitted only the bronze yue tube. When accumulated to form the Jialiang, then the sound matched Huangzhong and the pitch foundation was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Cai Yong's bronze yue tube truly preserved the surviving model of the Rites of Zhou. Yong himself was a master of pitch, which is why he transmitted only the bronze yue tube: once it was accumulated into the Jialiang, the sound matched Huangzhong and the foundation of pitch was established.

sentences.zh: 謂管有大小長短者，蓋嘉量既成，即以量聲定尺明矣。

translations.literal: Those who speak of pipes having different sizes and lengths — once the Jialiang is completed, using the measure's sound to fix the ruler is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Those who argue that pipes differ in size and length miss the point: once the Jialiang is complete, the measure's sound itself fixes the ruler, and the principle is plain.

sentences.zh: 今議者但爭《漢志》黍尺無準之法，殊不知鍾有鈞、石、量、衡之製。

translations.literal: Now the debaters only argue over the millet-measure method of the Han Treatise with no standard, yet do not know that bells have the systems of tuning weights, stone weights, measures, and balances.
translations.idiomatic: Today's debaters quarrel only over the Han Treatise's millet-measure method, which lacks a fixed standard, and fail to see that bell tones rest on integrated systems of tuning weights, stone weights, measures, and balances.

sentences.zh: 況《周禮》、《國語》，姬代聖經，翻謂無憑，孰為稽古？

translations.literal: Moreover the Rites of Zhou and the Discourses of the States are sacred classics of the Ji dynasty — to turn and say they have no basis, what is called examining antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou and the Discourses of the States are sacred classics of the Zhou house; to dismiss them as groundless is hardly what anyone would call examining antiquity.

sentences.zh: 有唐張文收定樂，亦鑄銅甌，此足驗周之嘉量以聲定律明矣。

translations.literal: In Tang, Zhang Wenshou fixed the music and also cast bronze ou vessels — this suffices to verify that the Zhou Jialiang, using sound to fix pitch, is clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tang dynasty, Zhang Wenshou fixed the music and also cast bronze ou vessels — enough proof that the Zhou Jialiang established pitch through sound, as the principle requires.

sentences.zh: 臣所以獨執《周禮》鑄嘉量者，以其方尺深尺，則度可見也；

translations.literal: The reason your subject alone holds to casting the Jialiang of the Rites of Zhou is that with its one square foot in breadth and one foot in depth, the standard of length is visible;
translations.idiomatic: I insist on casting the Jialiang according to the Rites of Zhou because, with its one square foot across and one foot deep, the standard of length is made visible;

sentences.zh: 其容一鬴，則量右見也；

translations.literal: with its capacity of one fu, the right measure is visible;
translations.idiomatic: with its capacity of one fu, the proper measure is visible;

sentences.zh: 其重鈞，則衡可見也；

translations.literal: with its weight of one jun, the balance is visible;
translations.idiomatic: with its weight of one jun, the standard of balance is visible;

sentences.zh: 聲中黃鍾之宮，則律可見也。

translations.literal: when it sounds the palace tone of Huangzhong, the pitch standard is visible.
translations.idiomatic: when it sounds the palace tone of Huangzhong, the pitch standard itself is visible.

sentences.zh: 既律、度、量、衡如此符合，則製管歌聲，其中必矣。

translations.literal: Since pitch, length, measure, and weight accord thus, then in making pipes and singing voice, the centering is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Once pitch, length, measure, and weight align in this way, pipes and song will necessarily fall into true pitch.

sentences.zh: 臣昧死欲乞將臣見鑄成銅甌，再限半月內更鑄嘉量，以其聲中黃鍾之宮，乃取李照新鍾就加修整，務合周製鍾量法度。

translations.literal: Your subject, risking death, wishes to beg that the bronze ou I have already cast be used; within another half month cast the Jialiang anew; using its sound matching the palace tone of Huangzhong, then take Li Zhao's new bell and adjust and trim it, striving to accord with the Zhou system's bell and measure standards.
translations.idiomatic: At the risk of my life, I beg permission to use the bronze ou I have already cast, and within another fortnight to cast a new Jialiang. Once its sound matches the palace tone of Huangzhong, Li Zhao's new bell should be adjusted and trimmed until it conforms to the Zhou system's standards for bells and measures.

sentences.zh: 文字已編寫次，未敢具進。”

translations.literal: The text has already been compiled in sequence, but I dare not submit it in full yet."
translations.idiomatic: The written account has already been drafted in order, but I have not yet dared to submit it in full."

sentences.zh: 詔送度等並定以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that it be sent to Du and the others together for determination and report.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the memorial sent to Ding Du and the others for joint review and report.

sentences.zh: 十月，度等言：“據鄧保信黍尺二，其一稱用上黨黍圓者一黍之長，累百成尺，與蔡邕合。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Du and the others said: "According to Deng Baoxin's second millet-measure standard, one of them is called using the length of one round Shangdang millet grain, accumulating a hundred to make a foot — this accords with Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Ding Du and his colleagues reported: "According to Deng Baoxin's second millet-measure standard, one version uses the length of a single round Shangdang millet grain, accumulated a hundred times to make a foot — and this agrees with Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 臣等檢詳前代造尺，皆以一黍之廣為分，唯後魏公孫崇以一黍之長累為寸法，太常劉芳以黍中者一黍之廣即為一分，中尉元匡以一黍之廣度黍二縫以取一分，三家競不能決。

translations.literal: Your subjects examined in detail the rulers made in previous generations — all used the width of one millet grain as a fen; only Gongsun Chong of Later Wei used the length of one millet grain accumulated as the inch method; Director of Ceremonies Liu Fang used the width of one middle millet grain as one fen; Commandant of Guards Yuan Kuang used the width of one millet grain measured across two gaps to obtain one fen — the three schools competing could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: We examined how rulers were made in earlier ages. All used the width of one millet grain as a fen, except that Gongsun Chong of Later Wei accumulated millet lengths to define inches; Liu Fang, Director of Ceremonies, took the width of one middling millet grain as one fen; and Yuan Kuang, Commandant of Guards, measured one millet grain across two gaps to obtain one fen. The three schools disputed one another and could not settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 而蔡邕銅龠，本誌中亦不明言用黍長廣累尺。

translations.literal: Yet in the original records of Cai Yong's bronze yue tube, it is also not clearly stated that millet length or width was accumulated to make a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the original records of Cai Yong's bronze yue tube, there is no clear statement that a foot was built up by accumulating millet length or width.

sentences.zh: 今將保信黃鍾管內黍二百粒以黍長為分，再累至尺二條，比保信元尺一長五黍，一長七黍，又律管黃鍾龠一枚，容黍千二百粒，以元尺比量，分寸略同。

translations.literal: Now taking two hundred millet grains inside Deng Baoxin's Huangzhong pipe, using millet length as fen and accumulating again to two one-foot strips — compared with Deng Baoxin's original foot, one is five grains longer and one seven grains longer. Also one Huangzhong yue pitch pipe holds twelve hundred millet grains; compared and measured with the original foot, the fen and cun are roughly the same.
translations.idiomatic: We took the two hundred millet grains inside Deng Baoxin's Huangzhong pipe, used millet length as the fen unit, and accumulated them into two one-foot strips. Compared with Deng Baoxin's original foot, one strip was five grains longer and one seven grains longer. A single Huangzhong yue pitch pipe, moreover, holds twelve hundred millet grains; measured against the original foot, its fen and cun divisions were roughly the same.

sentences.zh: 復將實龠黍再累者校之，即又不同。

translations.literal: Then comparing again with those accumulated from actual yue millet grains, they again differed.
translations.idiomatic: When we checked again against a foot built up from the actual millet grains of the yue tube, the results differed once more.

sentences.zh: 其龠、合、升、鬥亦皆類此。

translations.literal: The yue, he, sheng, and dou were all similar in this regard.
translations.idiomatic: The yue, he, sheng, and dou vessels all showed the same kind of discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 又阮逸、胡瑗鍾律法黍尺，其一稱用上黨羊頭山黍中者累廣求尺，製黃鍾之聲。

translations.literal: Also Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan's bell-pitch-law millet-measure standard — one is called using Shangdang Yangtoushan middle millet grains accumulated by width to seek the foot, making the sound of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan's millet-measure standard for bell pitch law likewise had one version that accumulated the width of middling millet grains from Shangdang's Yangtoushan to obtain a foot and produce the Huangzhong tone.

sentences.zh: 臣等以其大黍百粒累廣成尺，復將管內二百粒以黍廣為分，再累至尺二條，比逸等元尺一短七黍，一短三黍。

translations.literal: Your subjects, using a hundred large millet grains accumulated by width to make a foot, then taking two hundred grains inside the pipe using millet width as fen and accumulating again to two one-foot strips — compared with Yi and the others' original foot, one was seven grains shorter and one three grains shorter.
translations.idiomatic: We accumulated a hundred large millet grains by width to make a foot, then took the two hundred grains inside the pipe, used millet width as the fen unit, and built two one-foot strips. Compared with Ruan Yi and his colleagues' original foot, one strip was seven grains shorter and one three grains shorter.

sentences.zh: 蓋逸等元尺並用一等大黍，其實管之黍大小不均，遂致差異。

translations.literal: This is because Yi and the others' original foot both used one grade of large millet; in fact the millet grains in the pipe varied in size unevenly, thus causing the differences.
translations.idiomatic: This happened because Ruan Yi and his colleagues' original foot used only one grade of large millet, whereas the grains actually inside the pipe varied unevenly in size, which produced the discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 又其銅律管十二枚，臣等據楚衍等圍九方分之法，與逸等元尺及所實龠黍再累成尺者校之，又各不同。

translations.literal: Also their twelve bronze pitch pipes — your subjects, according to Chu Yan and others' method of circumference nine and square fen, compared them with Yi and the others' original foot and those accumulated from actual yue millet to make a foot — again each differed.
translations.idiomatic: Their twelve bronze pitch pipes, moreover, were checked by us according to Chu Yan's method of circumference nine and square fen against Ruan Yi's original foot and against feet built up from the actual yue millet grains — and again none agreed.

sentences.zh: 又所製銅稱二量亦皆類此。

translations.literal: Also the two copper balance weights they made were all similar in this regard.
translations.idiomatic: The two copper balance weights they made showed the same problem throughout.

sentences.zh: 臣等看詳其鍾、磬各一架，雖合典故，而黍尺一差，難以定奪。”

translations.literal: Your subjects examined in detail their one frame each of bells and chime-stones — though they accorded with classical precedent, yet one deviation in the millet-measure foot made it hard to decide definitively."
translations.idiomatic: We reviewed their one frame each of bells and chime-stones. Although they accorded with classical precedent, a single discrepancy in the millet-measure foot made a final judgment impossible."

sentences.zh: 又言：“太祖皇帝嚐詔和峴等用景表尺典修金石，七十年間，薦之郊廟，稽合唐製，以示詒謀。

translations.literal: They also said: "Emperor Taizu once ordered He Ning and others to use the shadow-table standard to canonically repair metal and stone instruments. Over seventy years they were recommended at suburban and temple altars, verified against Tang practice, to show guidance for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "Emperor Taizu once ordered He Ning and others to use the shadow-table standard in the canonical repair of metal and stone instruments. For seventy years those instruments were used at suburban and temple altars, checked against Tang practice, as guidance for posterity.

sentences.zh: 則可且依景表舊尺，俟天下有妙達鍾律之學者，俾考正之，以從周、漢之製。

translations.literal: Then for the present one may provisionally follow the old shadow-table standard, and wait until throughout the realm there is one skillfully versed in bell-pitch learning, and commission correction to follow the Zhou and Han systems.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, the court may provisionally follow the old shadow-table standard and wait until someone in the realm truly masters bell-pitch learning, then commission a correction to restore the Zhou and Han systems.

sentences.zh: 其阮逸、胡瑗、鄧保信並李照所用太府寺等尺及阮逸狀進《周禮》度量法，其說疏舛，不可依用。”

translations.literal: As for Ruan Yi, Hu Yuan, Deng Baoxin, and also Li Zhao's use of Grand Treasury Bureau and other standards, and Ruan Yi's memorial presenting the Rites of Zhou measure methods — their explanations are loose and erroneous and cannot be followed or used."
translations.idiomatic: The standards used by Ruan Yi, Hu Yuan, Deng Baoxin, and Li Zhao from the Grand Treasury Bureau and elsewhere, together with Ruan Yi's memorial presenting the Rites of Zhou measure methods, are loose and mistaken and should not be adopted."

sentences.zh: 五年五月，右司諫韓琦言：“臣前奉詔詳定鍾律，嚐覽《景祐廣樂記》，睹照所造樂不依古法，皆率己意別為律度，朝廷因而施用，識者非之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, Right Remonstrating Censor Han Qi said: "Your subject previously received the edict to examine in detail the pitch standards, and once perused the Records of Jingyou Broad Music, and saw that the music Zhao made did not follow ancient methods but followed his own ideas to establish separate pitch measures. The court thereupon adopted them, and those with knowledge criticized it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, Right Remonstrating Censor Han Qi memorialized: "When I was previously ordered to review the pitch standards, I read the Records of Jingyou Broad Music and found that the music Li Zhao made did not follow ancient methods but followed his own ideas in setting separate pitch measures. The court adopted it anyway, and informed observers objected.

sentences.zh: 今將親祀南郊，不可重以違古之樂上薦天地、宗廟。

translations.literal: Now the emperor will personally sacrifice at the Southern Suburban Altar — one cannot again use music that violates antiquity to offer to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is about to sacrifice personally at the Southern Suburban Altar. We cannot again offer Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples music that departs from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 竊聞太常舊樂見有存者，郊廟大禮，請復用之。”

translations.literal: I have heard that former music of the Court of Ceremonies still exists; for the great suburban and temple rites, please restore its use."
translations.idiomatic: I understand that portions of the Court of Ceremonies' former music still survive. For the great suburban and temple rites, I ask that they be restored."

sentences.zh: 詔資政殿大學士宋綬、三司使晏殊同兩製官詳定以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Academician Song Shou of the Hall of Resources for Governance and Fiscal Commissioner Yan Shu, together with officials of the Two Drafting Offices, to examine in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Grand Academician Song Shou of the Hall of Resources for Governance and Fiscal Commissioner Yan Shu, together with officials of the Two Drafting Offices, to review the matter and report.

sentences.zh: 七月，綬等言：“李照新樂比舊樂下三律，眾論以為無所考據。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Shou and the others said: "Li Zhao's new music is three pitch steps lower than the old music; popular opinion holds there is no basis for it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Song Shou and his colleagues reported: "Li Zhao's new music is three pitch steps lower than the old music, and public opinion holds that it lacks any authoritative basis.

sentences.zh: 願如琦請，郊廟復用和峴所定舊樂，鍾磬不經鐫磨者猶存三縣奇七虡，郊廟、殿庭可以更用。”

translations.literal: We wish, as Qi requested, that suburban and temple rites restore use of the old music fixed by He Ning. Bells and chime-stones not yet chiseled or filed still survive — three suspended sets plus seven ju stands — and may be used again at suburban altars, temple altars, and court halls."
translations.idiomatic: As Han Qi requested, we ask that suburban and temple rites restore the old music fixed by He Ning. Bells and chime-stones that have not been chiseled or filed still survive in three complete suspended sets plus seven ju frames, and these may again be used at suburban altars, temple altars, and palace courts."

sentences.zh: 太常亦言：“舊樂，宮縣用龍鳳散鼓四面，以應樂節，李照廢而不用，止以晉鼓一面應節。

translations.literal: The Court of Ceremonies also said: "In the old music, the palace ensemble used dragon-phoenix scattered drums on four sides to match the musical beats; Li Zhao abolished them and did not use them, using only one Jin drum on one side to match the beat.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Ceremonies added: "In the old music, the palace ensemble used dragon-and-phoenix scattered drums on four sides to mark the musical beats. Li Zhao abolished them and used only a single Jin drum on one side to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: 舊樂，建鼓四，並鞞、應共十二面，備而不擊，李照以四隅建鼓與鎛鍾相應擊之。

translations.literal: In the old music, there were four established drums, together with side and answering drums — twelve faces in all, complete but not struck; Li Zhao had the four corner established drums strike in response with the bofu bells.
translations.idiomatic: In the old music there were four established drums, together with side and answering drums — twelve faces in all, kept in readiness but not struck. Li Zhao had the four corner established drums struck in alternation with the bofu bells.

sentences.zh: 舊樂，雷鼓兩架各八面，止用一人考擊，李照別造雷鼓，每麵各用一人椎鼓，順天左旋，三步一止，又令二人搖鞉以應之。

translations.literal: In the old music, thunder drums — two frames each of eight faces — used only one person to examine and strike; Li Zhao separately made thunder drums, each face using one person to beat the drum, turning left with heaven, three steps one stop, and also ordered two people to shake tao to respond.
translations.idiomatic: In the old music, thunder drums stood in two frames of eight faces each, with only one person assigned to conduct and strike them. Li Zhao made new thunder drums and assigned one drummer to each face, turning left with the heavens, stopping every three steps, and also ordered two men to shake tao drums in response.

sentences.zh: 又所造大竽、大笙、雙鳳管、兩儀琴、十二弦琴並行。

translations.literal: Also the large yu, large sheng, double phoenix pipes, liangyi qin, and twelve-string qin were all used together.
translations.idiomatic: He also introduced large yu, large sheng, double phoenix pipes, liangyi qin, and twelve-string qin, all used together.

sentences.zh: 今既復用舊樂，未審照所作樂器制度，合改與否？”

translations.literal: Now that the old music is restored, we do not yet know whether the instruments Zhao made should be altered or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that the old music is to be restored, should the instruments Li Zhao devised be altered, or not?"

sentences.zh: 詔：“悉仍舊制，其李照所作，勿復施用。”

translations.literal: Edict: "All fully revert to the old system; as for what Li Zhao made, do not again use it."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Everything is to follow the old system. What Li Zhao made must not be used again."

sentences.zh: 康定元年，阮逸上《鍾律製議》並圖三卷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, Ruan Yi presented the Discourse on Making Pitch Standards together with three volumes of diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangding 1, Ruan Yi submitted his Discourse on Making Pitch Standards, together with three volumes of diagrams.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年五月，明堂禮儀使言：“明堂所用樂皆當隨月用律，九月以無射為均，五天帝各用本音之樂。”

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Huangyou, the Commissioner of Bright Hall Rites said: "The music used at the Bright Hall should all follow the monthly pitch law; in the ninth month Wushe is the key, and each of the Five Heavenly Emperors uses music of its own tone."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Huangyou 2, the Commissioner of Bright Hall Rites reported: "The music used in the Bright Hall should follow the pitch law of each month. In the ninth month Wushe serves as the key, and each of the Five Heavenly Emperors should use music in its own proper tone."

sentences.zh: 於是內出明堂樂曲及二舞名：迎神曰《誠安》；

translations.literal: Thereupon from within the palace were issued Bright Hall musical pieces and the names of two dances: for welcoming the spirits, "Cheng An";
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the palace issued the Bright Hall musical pieces and the names of two dances: for welcoming the spirits, "Cheng An";

sentences.zh: 皇帝升降行止曰《儀安》；

translations.literal: for the emperor's ascent, descent, going, and stopping, "Yi An";
translations.idiomatic: for the emperor's ascent, descent, movement, and pauses, "Yi An";

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝、皇地祇、神州地祇位奠玉幣曰《鎮安》，酌獻曰《慶安》；

translations.literal: for placing jade silks at the seats of August Heaven, August Earth, and the Spirit Lord of the Central Land, "Zhen An"; for libation offering, "Qing An";
translations.idiomatic: for placing jade silks at the seats of August Heaven, August Earth, and the Spirit Lord of the Central Land, "Zhen An"; for libation offerings, "Qing An";

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗、真宗位奠幣曰《信安》，酌獻曰《孝安》，司徒奉俎曰《饎安》；

translations.literal: for placing silks at the seats of Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong, "Xin An"; for libation offering, "Xiao An"; for the Minister of Education presenting the sacrificial meat, "Chi An";
translations.idiomatic: for placing silks at the seats of Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong, "Xin An"; for libation offerings, "Xiao An"; for the Minister of Education presenting the sacrificial meat, "Chi An";

sentences.zh: 五帝位奠玉幣曰《鎮安》，酌獻曰《精安》，皇帝飲福曰《胙安》；

translations.literal: for placing jade silks at the seats of the Five Emperors, "Zhen An"; for libation offering, "Jing An"; for the emperor drinking the blessing, "Zuo An";
translations.idiomatic: for placing jade silks at the seats of the Five Emperors, "Zhen An"; for libation offerings, "Jing An"; for the emperor drinking the blessing, "Zuo An";

sentences.zh: 退文舞、迎武舞、亞獻、終獻皆曰《穆安》，徹豆曰《歆安》，送神曰《誠安》歸大次曰《憩安》；

translations.literal: for withdrawing the civil dance, welcoming the martial dance, secondary offering, and final offering, all "Mu An"; for removing the beans, "Xin An"; for sending off the spirits, "Cheng An"; for returning to the great tent, "Qi An";
translations.idiomatic: for withdrawing the civil dance, welcoming the martial dance, the secondary offering, and the final offering, all "Mu An"; for removing the beans, "Xin An"; for sending off the spirits, "Cheng An"; for returning to the great tent, "Qi An";

sentences.zh: 文舞曰《右文化俗》，武舞曰《威功睿德》。

translations.literal: The civil dance was called "Right Culture Transforming Custom"; the martial dance was called "August Merit Wise Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance was titled "Right Culture Transforming Custom"; the martial dance was titled "August Merit and Wise Virtue."

sentences.zh: 又出禦撰樂章《鎮安》、《慶安》、《信安》、《孝安》四曲，餘詔輔臣分撰。

translations.literal: Also issued were four pieces of the imperially composed hymns — "Zhen An," "Qing An," "Xin An," and "Xiao An"; the remainder were ordered to auxiliary ministers to compose separately.
translations.idiomatic: The palace also issued four imperially composed hymn texts — "Zhen An," "Qing An," "Xin An," and "Xiao An" — and ordered the remaining texts distributed among senior ministers for separate composition.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔：“禦所撰樂曲名與常祀同者，更之。”

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, an edict said: "Where the names of the imperially composed musical pieces are the same as those for regular sacrifices, change them."
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, an edict ordered: "Where the names of the imperially composed musical pieces duplicate those used in regular sacrifices, they are to be changed."

sentences.zh: 遂更常所用圜丘寓祭明堂《誠安之曲》曰《宗安》，祀感生帝《慶安》之曲曰《光安》，奉慈廟《信安之曲》曰《慈安》。

translations.literal: Thereupon changed: the "Cheng An" hymn regularly used for the Round Mound vicarious sacrifice at Bright Hall was renamed "Zong An"; the "Qing An" hymn for sacrificing to the Emperor of Generative Life was renamed "Guang An"; the "Xin An" hymn for the Ci Temple was renamed "Ci An."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the "Cheng An" hymn regularly used when the Round Mound sacrifice was performed by proxy at the Bright Hall was renamed "Zong An"; the "Qing An" hymn for the sacrifice to the Emperor of Generative Life became "Guang An"; and the "Xin An" hymn for the Ci Temple became "Ci An."

sentences.zh: 六月，內出禦撰明堂樂八曲，以君、臣、民、事、物配屬五音，凡二十聲為一曲；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, from within the palace were issued eight imperially composed Bright Hall musical pieces, assigning ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things to the five tones — in all twenty notes making one piece;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the palace issued eight imperially composed Bright Hall pieces. Ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things were assigned to the five tones, with twenty notes forming one piece;

sentences.zh: 用宮變、徵變者，天、地、人、四時為七音，凡三十聲為一曲；

translations.literal: where using gong mutation and zhi mutation — heaven, earth, man, and the four seasons as seven tones — in all thirty notes making one piece;
translations.idiomatic: where gong mutation and zhi mutation were used, heaven, earth, man, and the four seasons formed seven tones, with thirty notes making one piece;

sentences.zh: 以子母相生，凡二十八聲為一曲：皆黃鍾為均。

translations.literal: using mother-son mutual generation — in all twenty-eight notes making one piece: all with Huangzhong as the key.
translations.idiomatic: using mother-and-son mutual generation, twenty-eight notes formed one piece — all with Huangzhong as the key.

sentences.zh: 又明堂月律五十七聲為二曲，皆無射為均；

translations.literal: Also Bright Hall monthly pitch law — fifty-seven notes making two pieces, all with Wushe as the key;
translations.idiomatic: There were also two Bright Hall pieces based on the monthly pitch law, of fifty-seven notes each, all with Wushe as the key;

sentences.zh: 又以二十聲、二十八聲、三十聲為三曲，亦無射為均，皆自黃鍾宮入無射。

translations.literal: also using twenty notes, twenty-eight notes, and thirty notes as three pieces, also with Wushe as the key — all entering Wushe from Huangzhong palace.
translations.idiomatic: and three further pieces of twenty, twenty-eight, and thirty notes, likewise with Wushe as the key, all proceeding from Huangzhong palace into Wushe.

sentences.zh: 如合用四十八或五十七聲，即依前譜次第成曲，其徹聲自同本律。

translations.literal: If suitable to use forty-eight or fifty-seven notes, then according to the preceding score in sequence complete the piece; the ending note naturally matches the same pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Where forty-eight or fifty-seven notes were required, the piece was completed in sequence according to the preceding score, with the closing note naturally matching its root pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 及禦撰鼓吹、警嚴曲、合宮歌並肄於太常。

translations.literal: And the imperially composed drum-and-pipe music, guard-of-honor pieces, and combined palace songs were all rehearsed at the Court of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The imperially composed drum-and-pipe music, guard-of-honor pieces, and combined palace songs were all rehearsed at the Court of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 是月，翰林學士承旨王堯臣等言：

translations.literal: That month, Hanlin Academician Chief Wang Yao and others said:
translations.idiomatic: That same month, Hanlin Academician Chief Wang Yao and his colleagues reported:

sentences.zh: 奉詔與參議阮逸所上編鍾四清聲譜法，請用之於明堂者。

translations.literal: Having received the edict to consult with Ruan Yi on the submitted method for the score of the four qing tones of the arranged bells, requesting its use at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: We were ordered to consult on Ruan Yi's submitted method for scoring the four qing tones of the arranged bells, which he proposed for use in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 竊以律呂旋宮之法既定以管，又製十二鍾準為十二正聲，以律計自倍半。

translations.literal: We consider that once the method of rotating the palace through the pitch tubes is fixed by the pipe, one also makes twelve bell standards as twelve primary tones, counting by pitch from double and half.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that once the method of rotating the palace through the pitch tubes is established by the pipe, twelve bell standards are also made as twelve primary tones, calculated by pitch in double and half relations.

sentences.zh: 說者云：“半者，準正聲之半，以為十二子聲之鍾，故有正聲、子聲各十二。”

translations.literal: Those who explain say: "Half means half of the primary-tone standard, to serve as the twelve zi-tone bells; thus there are twelve primary tones and twelve zi tones each."
translations.idiomatic: Expositors say: "By 'half' is meant half of the primary-tone standard, used to make the twelve zi-tone bells. Thus there are twelve primary tones and twelve zi tones."

sentences.zh: 子聲即清聲也。

translations.literal: The zi tone is the qing tone.
translations.idiomatic: The zi tone is the qing tone.

sentences.zh: 其正管長者為均，自用正聲；

translations.literal: Where the primary pipe is long, that is the key — use the primary tone by itself;
translations.idiomatic: When the primary pipe is long and serves as the key, the primary tone alone is used;

sentences.zh: 正管短者為均，則通用子聲而成五音。

translations.literal: where the primary pipe is short as key, then generally use the zi tone to complete the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: when the primary pipe is short and serves as the key, the zi tones are used generally to complete the five tones.

sentences.zh: 然求聲之法，本之於鍾，故《國語》所謂“度律均鍾”者也。

translations.literal: Yet the method of seeking tones is rooted in the bell; thus what the Discourses of the States calls "measuring pitch and tuning bells."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the method of deriving tones is rooted in the bell — hence the Discourses of the States speaks of "measuring pitch and tuning bells."

sentences.zh: 其編金石之法，則曆代不同，或以十九為一虡者，蓋取十二鍾當一月之辰，又加七律焉；

translations.literal: As for the method of arranging metal and stone — it differed by generation; some use nineteen for one ju — taking twelve bells corresponding to the months of the year, adding seven pitch steps;
translations.idiomatic: The method of arranging metal and stone instruments differed from age to age. Some used nineteen bells for one ju frame — taking twelve bells to match the months of the year and adding seven pitch steps;

sentences.zh: 或以二十一為一虡者，以一均聲更加濁倍；

translations.literal: some use twenty-one for one ju — adding one muddy double to a key tone;
translations.idiomatic: some used twenty-one for one ju, adding one muddy double to a key tone;

sentences.zh: 或以十六為一虡者，以一均清、正為十四，宮、商各置一，是謂“縣八用七”也；

translations.literal: some use sixteen for one ju — using qing and primary of one key as fourteen, placing one each for gong and shang — this is called "eight suspended using seven";
translations.idiomatic: some used sixteen for one ju, taking qing and primary tones of one key as fourteen and placing one each for gong and shang — this is what is meant by "eight suspended using seven";

sentences.zh: 或以二十四為一虡，則清、正之聲備。

translations.literal: some use twenty-four for one ju — then qing and primary tones are complete.
translations.idiomatic: some used twenty-four for one ju, in which qing and primary tones were fully provided.

sentences.zh: 故唐製以十六數為小架，二十四為大架，天地、宗廟、朝會各有所施。

translations.literal: Therefore the Tang system used sixteen for a small frame and twenty-four for a large frame; Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and court assemblies each had its application.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Tang system used sixteen bells for a small frame and twenty-four for a large frame, with separate arrangements for rites to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 今太常鍾縣十六者，舊傳正聲之外有黃鍾至夾鍾四清聲，雖於圖典未明所出，然考之實有義趣。

translations.literal: Now the Court of Ceremonies bell frame of sixteen — by old transmission beyond the primary tones there are four qing tones from Huangzhong to Jiazhong; though the canonical diagrams do not clearly state their origin, examination shows there is real rationale.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Ceremonies' sixteen-bell frame, by old transmission, includes four qing tones from Huangzhong to Jiazhong beyond the primary tones. Although canonical diagrams do not clearly explain their origin, examination shows real rationale behind them.

sentences.zh: 蓋自夷則至應鍾四律為均之時，若盡用正聲，則宮輕而商重，緣宮聲以下，不容更有濁聲。

translations.literal: For when the four pitch steps from Yize to Yingzhong serve as keys — if one used only primary tones throughout, gong would be light and shang heavy; since below gong tone there is no room for further muddy tones.
translations.idiomatic: When the four pitch steps from Yize to Yingzhong serve as keys, using only primary tones throughout makes gong light and shang heavy, for below gong there is no room for further muddy tones.

sentences.zh: 一均之中，宮弱商強，是謂陵僭，故須用子聲，乃得長短相敘。

translations.literal: Within one key, gong weak and shang strong — this is called overstepping hierarchy; therefore one must use zi tones to obtain long and short in proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single key, weak gong and strong shang constitute what is called overstepping proper rank; therefore zi tones must be used so that long and short tones fall into proper order.

sentences.zh: 自角而下，亦循茲法。

translations.literal: From jue downward, one also follows this method.
translations.idiomatic: From jue downward, the same principle applies.

sentences.zh: 故夷則為宮，則黃鍾為角；

translations.literal: Thus when Yize is gong, then Huangzhong is jue;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Yize serves as gong, Huangzhong serves as jue;

sentences.zh: 南呂為宮，則大呂為角；

translations.literal: when Nanlü is gong, then Dalü is jue;
translations.idiomatic: when Nanlü serves as gong, Dalü serves as jue;

sentences.zh: 無射為宮，則黃鍾為商、太簇為角；

translations.literal: when Wushe is gong, then Huangzhong is shang and Taicu is jue;
translations.idiomatic: when Wushe serves as gong, Huangzhong serves as shang and Taicu as jue;

sentences.zh: 應鍾為宮，則大呂為商、夾鍾為角。

translations.literal: when Yingzhong is gong, then Dalü is shang and Jiazhong is jue.
translations.idiomatic: when Yingzhong serves as gong, Dalü serves as shang and Jiazhong as jue.

sentences.zh: 蓋黃鍾、大呂、太簇、夾鍾正律俱長，並當用清聲，如此則音律相諧而無所抗，此四清聲可用之驗也。

translations.literal: For Huangzhong, Dalü, Taicu, and Jiazhong primary pitch steps are all long — all should use qing tones; thus pitch and tones harmonize without conflict — this is the verification that these four qing tones may be used.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong, Dalü, Taicu, and Jiazhong are all long primary pitch steps and should therefore use qing tones. In this way pitch and tone harmonize without conflict — and this is the proof that these four qing tones may be used.

sentences.zh: 至他律為宮，其長短、尊卑自序者，不當更以清聲間之。

translations.literal: When other pitch steps serve as gong, where long and short, high and low order themselves, one should not further insert qing tones among them.
translations.idiomatic: When other pitch steps serve as gong and long and short, high and low already fall into proper order, qing tones should not be inserted among them.

sentences.zh: 自唐末世，樂文墜缺，考擊之法久已不傳。

translations.literal: From the late Tang the music texts fell away and were lost; the methods of examination and striking had long not been transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Tang, musical texts have been lost and the methods of examination and striking have long ceased to be transmitted.

sentences.zh: 今若使匏、土、絲、竹諸器盡求清聲，即未見其法。

translations.literal: Now if one were to have gourd, clay, silk, and bamboo instruments all seek qing tones — no method for this is yet seen.
translations.idiomatic: If gourd, clay, silk, and bamboo instruments were all required to produce qing tones, no established method for doing so is yet visible.

sentences.zh: 又據大樂諸工所陳，自磬、簫、琴、和、巢笙五器本有清聲，塤、篪、竽、築、瑟五器本無清聲，五弦阮、九弦琴則有太宗皇帝聖製譜法。

translations.literal: Also according to what the great music artisans stated — chime-stone, xiao, qin, he, and nest-sheng five instruments originally have qing tones; xun, chi, yu, zhu, and se five instruments originally lack qing tones; five-string ruan and nine-string qin have the sage compositions of Emperor Taizong's scoring methods.
translations.idiomatic: According to the great music artisans, chime-stone, xiao, qin, he, and nest-sheng originally possess qing tones; xun, chi, yu, zhu, and se originally lack them; and the five-string ruan and nine-string qin have scoring methods composed by Emperor Taizong himself.

sentences.zh: 至歌工引音極唱，止及黃鍾清聲。

translations.literal: As for singers reaching the extreme of voice in leading notes — they reach only to Huangzhong qing tone.
translations.idiomatic: As for singers carrying the melody to its highest pitch, they reach only to the qing tone of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，其清、正二聲既有典據，理當施用。

translations.literal: Your subjects consulted and discuss: since the two tones qing and primary have canonical basis, by reason they should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: After consultation, we hold that since qing and primary tones both have canonical authority, they should by right be applied.

sentences.zh: 自今大樂奏夷則以下四均正律為宮之時，商、角依次並用清聲，自餘八均盡如常法。

translations.literal: From now when great music plays the four keys below Yize with primary pitch steps as gong — shang and jue in sequence should all use qing tones; the remaining eight keys all follow the usual method.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever great music plays the four keys below Yize with primary pitch steps as gong, shang and jue should in sequence use qing tones; the remaining eight keys should follow the usual method.

sentences.zh: 至於絲、竹等諸器舊有清聲者，令隨鍾石教習；

translations.literal: As for silk, bamboo, and other instruments that originally had qing tones — order them to follow bells and stones in practice;
translations.idiomatic: As for silk, bamboo, and other instruments that originally possessed qing tones, they should be taught to follow the bells and stones in performance;

sentences.zh: 本無清聲者，未可創意求法，且當如舊。

translations.literal: those originally without qing tones — one cannot newly devise methods to seek them; for now follow the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: those that originally lacked qing tones cannot yet be made to produce them by newly devised methods and should for now remain as before.

sentences.zh: 惟歌者本用中聲，故夏禹以聲為律，明人皆可及。

translations.literal: Only singers originally use the middle tone; thus Yu of Xia used sound as pitch — showing that everyone can reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Singers, however, originally use the middle register; as Yu of Xia used human voice as the pitch standard, it is clear that everyone can reach it.

sentences.zh: 若強所不至，足累至和。

translations.literal: If one forces what cannot be reached, it suffices to burden perfect harmony.
translations.idiomatic: To force what cannot be reached would only impair perfect harmony.

sentences.zh: 請止以正聲作歌，應合諸器亦自是一音，別無差戾。

translations.literal: We request only using primary tones for songs; instruments that should match will also naturally be one tone — separately no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that songs use only primary tones; the instruments that should match them will naturally remain of one tone, with no separate discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 其阮逸所上聲譜，以清濁相應，先後互擊，取音靡曼，近於鄭聲，不可用。

translations.literal: The sound score Ruan Yi submitted — using qing and muddy in mutual response, striking alternately first and after, taking tones flowery and lingering, close to Zheng music — cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: The sound score Ruan Yi submitted, with qing and muddy tones answering one another and struck alternately in sequence, produces tones that are soft and lingering and approach the music of Zheng — and cannot be used.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: Edict: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 七月，禦撰明堂無射宮樂曲譜三，皆五十七字，五音一曲，奉俎用之；

translations.literal: In the seventh month, three imperially composed Bright Hall musical scores in the Wushe-gong mode were issued, each of fifty-seven notes — one piece in five tones, for presenting the sacrificial meat;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, the throne issued three imperially composed Bright Hall musical scores in the Wushe-gong mode, each of fifty-seven notes: one piece built from five tones, for the presentation of sacrificial meat;

sentences.zh: 二變七律一曲，飲福用之；

translations.literal: one piece with two mutations and seven tones, for drinking the blessing;
translations.idiomatic: one piece with two mutations and seven tones, for drinking the blessing wine;

sentences.zh: 七律相生一曲，退文舞、迎武舞及亞獻、終獻、徹豆用之。

translations.literal: one piece of seven tones generating one another, for withdrawing the civil dance, welcoming the martial dance, the secondary offering, final offering, and removing the beans.
translations.idiomatic: and one piece of seven mutually generating tones, for withdrawing the civil dance, welcoming the martial dance, the secondary and final offerings, and removing the bean dishes.

sentences.zh: 是月，上封事者言：“明堂酌獻五帝《精安之曲》，並用黃鍾一均聲，此乃國朝常祀、五時迎氣所用舊法，若於親行大饗，即所未安。

translations.literal: That month, one who submitted a sealed memorial said: "For libation offerings to the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall, the hymn 'Perfect Peace' — all use one key in Huangzhong pitch; this is the old method used in the dynasty's regular sacrifices and the five-season welcoming of qi. If applied to personally conducting the grand feast sacrifice, it is what brings no ease.
translations.idiomatic: That month, a memorialist submitted: "At the Bright Hall, the libation offerings to the Five Emperors use the hymn 'Perfect Peace,' all in a single Huangzhong key — the established method for the dynasty's regular sacrifices and the five-season welcoming of qi. For the emperor's personal performance of the grand feast sacrifice, this would be unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 且明堂之位，木室在寅，火室在巳，金室在申，水室在亥，蓋木、火、金、水之始也；

translations.literal: Moreover the positions at the Bright Hall — the Wood chamber is at yin, Fire at si, Metal at shen, Water at hai — roughly the beginnings of Wood, Fire, Metal, and Water;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the Bright Hall the Wood chamber stands at yin, the Fire chamber at si, the Metal chamber at shen, and the Water chamber at hai — marking the beginnings of Wood, Fire, Metal, and Water;

sentences.zh: 土室在西南，蓋土王之次也。

translations.literal: the Earth chamber is in the southwest — roughly the position where Earth reigns.
translations.idiomatic: the Earth chamber stands in the southwest, marking the season when Earth holds sway.

sentences.zh: 既皆用五行本始所王之次，則獻神之樂亦當用五行本始月律，各從其音以為曲。

translations.literal: Since all use the sequence of what the Five Phases originally govern, then the music for offering to the spirits should also use the monthly pitch pipes of the Five Phases' original beginnings, each following its tone to make a piece.
translations.idiomatic: Since the layout already follows the sequence in which the Five Phases originally hold sway, the offering music ought likewise to use the monthly pitch pipes of each Phase's original beginning, with each hymn composed in its corresponding tone.

sentences.zh: 其《精安》五曲，宜以無射之均；

translations.literal: Its five pieces of 'Perfect Peace' should use the Wushe key;
translations.idiomatic: The five 'Perfect Peace' hymns should be set in the Wushe key;

sentences.zh: 太簇為角，獻青帝；

translations.literal: Taichu as jue, offering to the Green Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: with Taichu as jue for the Green Emperor;

sentences.zh: 仲呂為徵，獻赤帝；

translations.literal: Zhonglü as zhi, offering to the Red Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü as zhi for the Red Emperor;

sentences.zh: 林鍾為宮，獻黃帝；

translations.literal: Linzhong as gong, offering to the Yellow Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Linzhong as gong for the Yellow Emperor;

sentences.zh: 夷則為商，獻白帝；

translations.literal: Yize as shang, offering to the White Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Yize as shang for the White Emperor;

sentences.zh: 應鍾為羽，獻黑帝。”

translations.literal: Yingzhong as yu, offering to the Black Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: and Yingzhong as yu for the Black Emperor."

sentences.zh: 詔兩製官同太常議，而堯臣等言：“大饗日迫，事難猝更。”

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials of the Two Drafting Offices together with the Court of Ceremonies to discuss; Yao Chen and others said: "The grand feast day is near — the matter is hard to change suddenly."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Two Drafting Offices and the Court of Ceremonies to deliberate together. Wang Yao Chen and others replied: "The grand feast is imminent, and the rite cannot be abruptly revised."

sentences.zh: 詔俟過大禮，詳定以聞。

translations.literal: An edict: wait until after the great ceremony, examine and fix in detail, and report.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: after the great ceremony, examine the matter fully and report.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝服靴袍，禦崇政殿，召近臣、宗室、館閣、台諫官閱雅樂，自宮架、登歌、舞佾之奏凡九十一曲遍作之，因出太宗琴、阮譜及禦撰明堂樂曲音譜，並按習大樂新錄，賜群臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the emperor, wearing boots and robe, proceeded to Chongzheng Hall, summoned close ministers, imperial clansmen, institute and pavilion scholars, and remonstrating censors to review elegant music — from the suspended ensemble, ascent singing, and dance rows, in all ninety-one pieces fully performed; thereupon issued Taizong's qin and ruan scores and the imperially composed Bright Hall musical pitch scores, and also rehearsed the newly recorded great music, bestowing these upon the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the emperor, dressed in boots and robe, proceeded to Chongzheng Hall and summoned close ministers, members of the imperial clan, institute and pavilion scholars, and remonstrating censors to review the court music. The suspended ensemble, ascent singing, and dance rows performed all ninety-one pieces in full. He then presented Taizong's qin and ruan scores and his own Bright Hall musical pitch scores, rehearsed the newly recorded great music, and bestowed them upon the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 又出新製頌塤、匏笙、洞簫，仍令登歌以八音諸器各奏一曲，遂召鼓吹局按警場，賜大樂、鼓吹令丞至樂工徒吏緡錢有差。

translations.literal: Also issued were newly made song xun, gourd sheng, and vertical flutes; still ordered ascent singing to use the eight categories of instruments each to play one piece; then summoned the drum-and-wind bureau to rehearse the guard field music, bestowing graded strings of cash on the directors and vice-directors of great music and drum-and-wind down to musicians, attendants, and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He also unveiled newly made song xun, gourd sheng, and vertical flutes, and had the ascent singers perform one piece on each instrument of the eight categories of sound. The drum-and-wind bureau was then summoned to rehearse the guard field music, and graded gifts of cash were bestowed on the directors and vice-directors of great music and drum-and-wind, down to the musicians, attendants, and clerks.

sentences.zh: 帝既閱雅樂，謂輔臣曰：“作樂崇德，薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had reviewed the elegant music, he said to his chief ministers: "Making music exalts virtue; offering it to August Heaven, to match the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: After reviewing the court music, the emperor said to his chief ministers: "Music is made to exalt virtue, offered to August Heaven, and paired with the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今將有事於明堂，然世鮮知音，其令太常並加講求。”

translations.literal: Now we are about to perform rites at the Bright Hall, yet the age rarely has those who understand pitch — order the Court of Ceremonies together to increase study and inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: We are about to perform rites at the Bright Hall, yet few in this age truly understand pitch. Order the Court of Ceremonies to pursue the matter with all diligence."

sentences.zh: 時言者以為鎛鍾、特磬未協音律，詔令鄧保信、阮逸、盧昭序同太常檢詳典禮，別行鑄造。

translations.literal: At the time critics held that the set bells and single chime-stones did not accord with pitch law; an edict ordered Deng Baoxin, Ruan Yi, and Lu Zhaoxu together with the Court of Ceremonies to examine the canonical rites in detail and cast anew separately.
translations.idiomatic: Critics at the time held that the set bells and single chime-stones did not accord with pitch law. An edict ordered Deng Baoxin, Ruan Yi, and Lu Zhaoxu, together with the Court of Ceremonies, to examine the canonical rites in detail and cast new instruments separately.

sentences.zh: 太常薦太子中舍致仕胡瑗曉音，詔同定鍾磬制度。

translations.literal: The Court of Ceremonies recommended the retired Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Hu Yuan, who understood pitch; an edict ordered him to fix the bell and chime-stone system together with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Ceremonies recommended Hu Yuan, a retired Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat versed in pitch, and an edict ordered him to join them in fixing the bell and chime-stone system.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，詔曰：“朕聞古者作樂，本以薦上帝、配祖考，三、五之盛，不相沿襲，然必太平，始克明備。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month, an edict said: "We have heard that in antiquity music was made fundamentally to offer to August Heaven and match the ancestors. The glories of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors did not follow one another in succession, yet only in great peace could it be made clear and complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month, an edict declared: "We have heard that in antiquity music was made above all to offer to August Heaven and pair with the ancestors. The glories of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors did not simply follow one upon another, yet only in ages of great peace could music be brought to full clarity and completion.

sentences.zh: 周武受命，至成王時始大合樂；

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou received the Mandate, yet only in King Cheng's time was music fully consolidated;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou received the Mandate, yet music was not fully consolidated until the reign of King Cheng;

sentences.zh: 漢初亦沿舊樂，至武帝時始定泰一、後土樂詩；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han they also followed the old music; only in Emperor Wu's time were the hymns of Grand Unity and Queen Earth fixed;
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han the court likewise followed the old music; only under Emperor Wu were the hymns of Grand Unity and Queen Earth established;

sentences.zh: 光武中興，至明帝時始改“大予”之名；

translations.literal: Guangwu restored the dynasty, yet only in Emperor Ming's time was the name 'Grandee' changed;
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, the name 'Grandee of Music' was not changed until the reign of Emperor Ming;

sentences.zh: 唐高祖造邦，至太宗時孝孫、文收始定鍾律，明皇方成唐樂。

translations.literal: Tang Gaozu founded the realm; only in Taizong's time did Xiaosun and Wenshou first fix bell pitch; Emperor Ming only then completed Tang music.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Gaozu founded the realm, yet bell pitch was not fixed until the reign of Taizong, when Zhang Xiaosun and Zhang Wenshou did so; only under Emperor Ming was Tang music fully completed.

sentences.zh: 是知經啟善述，禮樂重事，須三四世，聲文乃定。

translations.literal: From this one knows that opening through goodness and completing through transmission — rites and music are weighty matters; it requires three or four generations before sounds and texts are fixed.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that rites and music are weighty matters, opened through goodness and completed through transmission: three or four generations are needed before sounds and texts are truly fixed.

sentences.zh: 國初亦循用王樸、竇儼所定周樂，太祖患其聲高，遂令和峴減一律，真宗始議隨月轉律之法，屢加按核。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty they also followed the Zhou music fixed by Wang Pu and Dou Yan; Taizu was troubled that its pitch ran high and ordered He Ning to reduce one pitch step; Zhenzong first proposed the method of rotating pitch by month, repeatedly adding examination and verification.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding the court likewise followed the Zhou music established by Wang Pu and Dou Yan. Taizu found its pitch too high and ordered He Ning to lower it by one step. Zhenzong first proposed the method of rotating pitch by month, and the matter was repeatedly examined and verified.

sentences.zh: 然念《樂經》久墜，學者罕傳，曆古研覃，亦未究緒。

translations.literal: Yet reflecting that the Music Classic long ago fell away, scholars rarely transmit it — through the ages studied and pondered, yet its thread has not been fully traced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we reflect that the Music Classic has long been lost, and few scholars still transmit it; though the subject has been studied across the ages, its principles have never been fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 頃雖博加訪求，終未有知聲、知經可信之人。

translations.literal: Recently, though broadly adding inquiry and search, in the end there was still no one trustworthy who understood pitch and understood the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Although we have lately sought widely, we have still found no one trustworthy in both pitch and the classics.

sentences.zh: 嚐為改更，未適茲意。

translations.literal: Once revisions were attempted, yet they did not suit this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Revisions have been attempted before, yet none have satisfied our intent.

sentences.zh: 中書門下其集兩製及太常禮樂官，以天地、五方、神州、日月、宗廟、社蠟祭享所用登歌、宮縣，審定聲律是非，按古合今，調諧中和，使經久可用，以發揚祖宗之功德，朕何憚改為？

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Chancellery shall assemble officials of the Two Drafting Offices and the Court of Ceremonies' ritual and music officers, taking the ascent singing and suspended ensembles used in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Five Directions, the Central Land, sun and moon, ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain and seasonal rites — examine and fix whether the pitch laws are right or wrong, match antiquity with the present, harmonize to perfect harmony, make them enduringly usable, to spread abroad the merit and virtue of the ancestors — what would We shrink from changing?
translations.idiomatic: Let the Secretariat and Chancellery assemble officials of the Two Drafting Offices and the Court of Ceremonies' ritual and music officers to examine the ascent singing and suspended ensembles used in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Five Directions, the Central Land, sun and moon, ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain and seasonal rites — determine whether the pitch laws are sound or flawed, reconcile antiquity with the present, and harmonize them to perfect balance so that they may endure. To spread abroad the merit and virtue of the ancestors, what change would We hesitate to make?

sentences.zh: 但審聲、驗書，二學鮮並，互詆胸臆，無所援據，慨然希古，靡忘於懷。”

translations.literal: Only the two disciplines of examining pitch and verifying texts are rarely united; they mutually slander from their own breasts, with nothing to cite as basis — sighing, one longs for antiquity, never forgetting it in the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two disciplines of examining pitch and verifying texts are rarely united; their practitioners assail one another from private conviction, with nothing authoritative to cite. We sigh at this and long for antiquity, and the thought never leaves Our mind."

sentences.zh: 於是中書門下集兩製、太常官，置局於秘閣，詳定大樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat and Chancellery assembled officials of the Two Drafting Offices and the Court of Ceremonies, established an office in the Secret Repository, and examined and fixed the great music in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Secretariat and Chancellery assembled officials of the Two Drafting Offices and the Court of Ceremonies, established an office in the Secret Repository, and set about examining and fixing the great music in detail.

sentences.zh: 王堯臣等言：天章閣待制趙師民博通今古，願同祥定，及乞借參知政事高若訥所校十五等古尺。

translations.literal: Wang Yao Chen and others said: Palace Attendant-in-Waiting at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations Zhao Shimin is broadly versed in past and present and wishes to join in examining and fixing; also requesting to borrow the fifteen-rank ancient ruler collated by Vice Grand Councilor Gao Ruone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yao Chen and others reported that Zhao Shimin, Palace Attendant-in-Waiting at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, was broadly versed in past and present and wished to join the review, and asked to borrow the fifteen-rank ancient ruler collated by Vice Grand Councilor Gao Ruone.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，詔徐、宿、泗、耀、江、鄭、淮陽七州軍采磬石，仍令諸路轉運司訪民間有藏古尺律者上之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, an edict ordered the seven prefectures and military commissions of Xu, Su, Si, Yao, Jiang, Zheng, and Huaiyang to gather chime-stone, and still ordered the transport commissions of each circuit to seek among the people those who possessed ancient rulers and pitch pipes and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, an edict ordered the prefectures and military commissions of Xu, Su, Si, Yao, Jiang, Zheng, and Huaiyang to gather chime-stone, and directed the transport commissions of each circuit to seek out private owners of ancient rulers and pitch pipes and submit them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔兩製及禮官參稽典制，議定國朝大樂名，中書門下審加詳閱以聞。

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict ordered the Two Drafting Offices and ritual officers to consult canonical institutions, discuss and fix the name of the dynasty's great music, and the Secretariat and Chancellery to examine in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, an edict ordered the Two Drafting Offices and ritual officers to consult the canonical institutions and determine a name for the dynasty's great music; the Secretariat and Chancellery were to review the proposal in detail and report.

sentences.zh: 初，胡瑗請太祖廟舞用幹戚，太宗廟兼用幹、羽，真宗廟用羽、龠，以象三聖功德。

translations.literal: Initially, Hu Yuan requested that the dance at Taizu's temple use shields and axes, Taizong's temple use both shields and feathers, and Zhenzong's temple use feathers and yue pipes — to symbolize the merit and virtue of the three sage emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hu Yuan had proposed that the dance at Taizu's temple use shields and axes, at Taizong's temple both shields and feathers, and at Zhenzong's temple feathers and yue pipes, to symbolize the merit and virtue of the three sage emperors.

sentences.zh: 然議者謂國朝七廟之舞，名雖不同，而幹、羽並用，又廟製與古異。

translations.literal: Yet critics said that in the dances of the dynasty's seven ancestral temples, though the names differ, shields and feathers are used together, and moreover the temple system differs from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected, however, that although the dances of the dynasty's seven ancestral temples bore different names, shields and feathers were used together in all of them, and the temple system itself differed from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 及瑗建言，止降詔定樂名而已。

translations.literal: When Yuan submitted his proposal, only an edict fixing the music name was issued — nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan's proposal came forward, the throne issued only an edict fixing the music's name and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 七月，堯臣等言：“按太常天地、宗廟、四時之祀，樂章凡八十九曲，自《景安》而下七十五章，率以‘安’名曲，豈特本道德、政教嘉靖之美，亦緣神靈、祖考安樂之故。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Yao Chen and others said: "According to the Court of Ceremonies' sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and the four seasons, the hymn texts number eighty-nine pieces in all; from 'Prosperous Peace' downward, seventy-five sections — mostly naming pieces with 'Peace' — is this not only rooted in the beauty of virtue, governance, and flourishing teaching, but also because spirits and ancestors dwell in peace?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Wang Yao Chen and others reported: "According to the Court of Ceremonies, the hymn texts for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and the four seasons number eighty-nine pieces in all. From 'Prosperous Peace' downward, seventy-five sections are mostly named with 'Peace.' This reflects not only the beauty of virtue, governance, and flourishing teaching, but also the peace in which spirits and ancestors dwell.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹上議，國朝樂宜名《大安》。”

translations.literal: Your subjects respectfully submit the proposal that the dynasty's music should be named 'Great Peace.'"
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully propose that the dynasty's music should be named 'Great Peace.'"

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“朕惟古先格王隨代之樂，亦既製作，必有稱謂，緣名以討義，由義以知德，蓋名者，德之所載，有行遠垂久之效焉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We reflect that the music of successive dynasties under the ancient sage kings who measured and corrected — once made, there must be a designation; following the name to seek the meaning, from the meaning to know virtue — for names are what virtue carries, with the effect of reaching far and enduring long.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "We reflect that the music of successive dynasties under the ancient sage kings, once created, always received a name. From the name one seeks the meaning, and from the meaning one knows virtue; for a name is what virtue bears, and it has the power to reach far and endure.

sentences.zh: 故《韶》以紹堯，《夏》以承舜，《》以救民，《武》以象伐，傳之不朽，用此道也。

translations.literal: Thus 'Shao' to continue Yao, 'Xia' to succeed Shun, 'Shang' to save the people, 'Wu' to depict conquest — transmitted undying, by this way.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shao continued Yao, Xia succeeded Shun, Shang rescued the people, and Wu depicted conquest — they have been transmitted undying because they followed this principle.

sentences.zh: 國家舉墜正失，典章交備，獨斯體大而有司莫敢易言之。

translations.literal: The state raises what fell and corrects what was lost; institutions are fully complete — only this matter is great in scope, and the responsible officials dare not lightly speak of changing it.
translations.idiomatic: Our state has raised what had fallen and corrected what was lost until its institutions stand complete; yet this matter alone is so vast in scope that responsible officials have not dared lightly to propose a change.

sentences.zh: 朕憫然念茲，大懼列聖之休未能昭揭於天下之聽，是用申敕執事，還求博講而考定其衷。

translations.literal: We, moved, reflect on this and greatly fear that the blessings of the successive sages have not yet been clearly revealed to all under heaven's hearing — therefore reiterate command to the executors, again seeking broad discussion and examining and fixing the inner truth.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, We greatly fear that the blessings of the successive sage emperors have not yet been fully revealed to all the world. We therefore charged Our officers anew to seek broad counsel and determine the true meaning.

sentences.zh: 今禮官、學士迨三有事之臣，同寅一辭，以《大安》之議來復。

translations.literal: Now the ritual officers, academicians, and those charged with the three matters — with one accord speak as one voice, returning with the proposal of 'Great Peace.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the ritual officers, academicians, and those charged with these three matters speak with one accord, returning with the proposal of 'Great Peace.'

sentences.zh: 且謂：藝祖之戡暴亂也，安天下之未安，其功大；

translations.literal: Moreover it says: When the Founding Ancestor quelled violent disorder, securing what under Heaven was not yet secure, his merit was great;
translations.idiomatic: It went on to say that when the Founding Ancestor put down rebellion and brought peace to an unsettled realm, his achievement was supreme;

sentences.zh: 二宗之致太平也，安天下之既安，其德盛；

translations.literal: when the Two Ancestors brought great peace, securing what under Heaven was already secure, their virtue was sublime;
translations.idiomatic: that when the Two Ancestors achieved great peace and kept secure what was already secure, their virtue was sublime;

sentences.zh: 洎朕之承聖烈也，安祖宗之所安，其仁厚。

translations.literal: and now that I inherit the sacred achievements, securing what the ancestors secured, my benevolence is deep.
translations.idiomatic: and that now, as I inherit their sacred legacy and preserve what the ancestors preserved, my own benevolence runs deep.

sentences.zh: 祇覽所議，熟復於懷。

translations.literal: Reverently reviewing what was proposed, I have pondered it repeatedly in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Having reverently read what was proposed, I have turned it over again and again in my mind.

sentences.zh: 恭惟神德之造基，神功之戢武，章聖恢清淨之治，衝人蒙成定之業，雖因世之跡各異，而靖民之道同歸。

translations.literal: Reverently considering the divine virtue that laid the foundation, the divine martial achievement that stilled warfare, Emperor Zhang's expansion of pure and tranquil governance, and the young ruler's inheritance of the settled enterprise—although the traces left by each age differ, the way of pacifying the people converges in the same end.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect with reverence on the divine virtue that founded our house, the divine martial power that stilled the wars, Emperor Zhang's restoration of pure and tranquil rule, and the young emperor's inheritance of an already settled realm: though each age left its own mark, the path of bringing peace to the people leads to the same end.

sentences.zh: 以之播鍾球、文羽籥、用諸郊廟、告於神明，曰‘大’且‘安’，誠得其正。”

translations.literal: To spread this in bells and stone chimes, adorn with patterned feathers and flutes, use it in suburban and temple rites, and announce it to the spirits—calling it both "Great" and "Tranquil" truly hits the mark."
translations.idiomatic: To set this forth in bells and chimes, feathered banners and reed pipes, to use it in suburban and ancestral rites and proclaim it before the spirits—to call it both Great and Tranquil is indeed the right name."

sentences.zh: 十二月，召兩府及侍臣觀新樂於紫宸殿，凡鎛鍾十二：黃鍾高二尺二寸半，廣一尺二寸，鼓六，鉦四，舞六，甬、衡並旋蟲高八寸四分，遂徑一寸二分，深一寸一厘，篆帶每麵縱者四，橫者四，枚景挾鼓與舞，四處各有九，每麵共三十六，兩欒間一尺四寸，容九斗九升五合，重一百六斤；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Two Departments and attendant ministers were summoned to view the new music in the Hall of Purple Brightness. There were twelve bo bells in all: the Yellow Bell was two chi two and a half cun high and one chi two cun wide, with six drum sections, four zheng sections, and six dance sections; stem, crossbar, and spiral dragon ornament together stood eight cun four fen high; the nipple was one cun two fen in diameter and one cun one li deep; on the inscribed band each face had four vertical and four horizontal lines; bosses and cross-struts flanked the drum and dance sections, nine at each of four points, thirty-six per face; the distance between the two suspension bars was one chi four cun; capacity was nine dou nine sheng five he; weight was one hundred six jin;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Two Departments and attendant ministers were summoned to the Hall of Purple Brightness to hear the new music. There were twelve bo bells. The Yellow Bell stood two chi two and a half cun high and one chi two cun across, with six drum panels, four zheng panels, and six dance panels; stem, crossbar, and spiral-dragon finial together measured eight cun four fen; the nipple was one cun two fen across and one cun one li deep. On the inscribed band each face bore four vertical and four horizontal lines. Bosses and cross-struts bracketed the drum and dance panels—nine at each of four positions, thirty-six per face. The two suspension bars were one chi four cun apart. Capacity was nine dou nine sheng five he; weight, one hundred six jin.

sentences.zh: 大呂以下十一鍾並與黃鍾同製，而兩欒間遞減半分；

translations.literal: The eleven bells from Great Pipe downward shared the same design as the Yellow Bell, but the distance between the two suspension bars decreased by half a fen successively;
translations.idiomatic: The eleven bells from Great Pipe downward followed the Yellow Bell's design, but the gap between the two suspension bars shrank by half a fen at each step;

sentences.zh: 至應鍾容九斗三升五合，而其重加至應鍾重一百四十八斤；

translations.literal: at the Ying Bell the capacity was nine dou three sheng five he, and the weight increased successively until the Ying Bell weighed one hundred forty-eight jin;
translations.idiomatic: down to the Ying Bell, whose capacity was nine dou three sheng five he and whose weight rose step by step to one hundred forty-eight jin;

sentences.zh: 並中新律本律。

translations.literal: All matched the fundamental pitch of each note in the new pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Each bell struck true to its fundamental pitch under the new standard.

sentences.zh: 特磬十二：黃鍾、大呂股長二尺，博一尺，鼓三尺，博六寸九分寸之六，弦三尺七寸五分；

translations.literal: There were twelve special stone chimes: the Yellow Bell and Great Pipe had thighs two chi long and one chi wide, soundbows three chi long and six cun nine and six tenths of a fen wide, and suspension cords three chi seven and a half cun;
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve special stone chimes. For Yellow Bell and Great Pipe the thigh was two chi long and one chi wide, the soundbow three chi long and six cun nine and six-tenths of a fen wide, and the suspension cord three chi seven and a half cun;

sentences.zh: 太簇以下股長尺八寸，博九寸，鼓二尺七寸，博六寸，弦三尺三寸七分半，其聲各中本律。

translations.literal: From Major Third downward the thigh was one chi eight cun long and nine cun wide, the soundbow two chi seven cun long and six cun wide, and the suspension cord three chi three cun seven and a half fen; each note matched its fundamental pitch.
translations.idiomatic: From Major Third downward the thigh measured one chi eight cun by nine cun, the soundbow two chi seven cun by six cun, and the suspension cord three chi three cun seven and a half fen; each chime sounded its proper fundamental.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾厚二寸一分，大呂以下遞加其厚，至應鍾厚三寸五分。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell was two cun one fen thick; from Great Pipe downward the thickness increased successively, until the Ying Bell was three cun five fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell was two cun one fen thick; from Great Pipe down the chimes grew progressively thicker, reaching three cun five fen at the Ying Bell.

sentences.zh: 詔以其圖送中書。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the diagrams sent to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that the diagrams be sent to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 議者以為《周禮》：“大鍾十分其鼓間，以其一為之厚；

translations.literal: Commentators held that the Rites of Zhou says: "For a large bell, take one-tenth of the drum interval as its thickness;
translations.idiomatic: Commentators cited the Rites of Zhou: "For a large bell, one-tenth of the drum interval gives the thickness;

sentences.zh: 小鍾十分其鉦間，以其一為之厚。”

translations.literal: for a small bell, take one-tenth of the zheng interval as its thickness."
translations.idiomatic: for a small bell, one-tenth of the zheng interval gives the thickness."

sentences.zh: 則是大鍾宜厚，小鍾宜薄。

translations.literal: Thus the large bell should be thick and the small bell thin.
translations.idiomatic: By that rule the large bell ought to be thick and the small bell thin.

sentences.zh: 今大鍾重一百六斤，小鍾乃重一百四十八斤，則小鍾厚，非也。

translations.literal: Now the large bell weighs one hundred six jin while the small bell weighs one hundred forty-eight jin—so the small bell is thick, which is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet here the large bell weighs one hundred six jin and the small bell one hundred forty-eight—the small bell is the heavier one, which is wrong.

sentences.zh: 又：“磬氏為磬，倨句一矩有半，博為一，股為二，鼓為三。

translations.literal: Again: "The Chime Maker makes chimes with an obtuse angle of one and a half right angles; width is one, thigh two, soundbow three.
translations.idiomatic: They also cited: "The Chime Maker shapes chimes at an obtuse angle of one and a half right angles, with width as one, thigh as two, and soundbow as three.

sentences.zh: 參分其股博，去其一以為鼓博；

translations.literal: Divide the thigh width into three and take away one to get the soundbow width;
translations.idiomatic: Take two-thirds of the thigh's width for the soundbow's width;

sentences.zh: 三分其鼓博，以其一為之厚。”

translations.literal: divide the soundbow width into three and take one as the thickness."
translations.idiomatic: divide the soundbow width into three and take one part as the thickness."

sentences.zh: 今磬無博厚、無長短，亦非也。

translations.literal: Now the chimes have no differentiation in width and thickness or in length and shortness—this too is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these chimes show no gradation in width, thickness, or length—another error.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，命參知政事劉沆、梁適監議大樂。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, Vice Grand Councillors Liu Kang and Liang Shi were ordered to supervise deliberations on the great music.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year five, Vice Grand Councillors Liu Kang and Liang Shi were appointed to oversee the review of the great music.

sentences.zh: 是月，知制誥王洙奏：“黃鍾為宮最尊者，但聲有尊卑耳，不必在其形體也。

translations.literal: That month, Drafting Officer Wang Shu memorialized: "The Yellow Bell as gong is the most honored pitch, but this concerns only the high and low of sound, not necessarily the physical form.
translations.idiomatic: That month Drafting Officer Wang Shu submitted a memorial: "Yellow Bell as gong is the most exalted pitch, but that honor lies in the pitch itself, not in the instrument's size.

sentences.zh: 言鍾磬依律數為大小之製者，經典無正文，惟鄭康成立意言之，亦自雲假設之法。

translations.literal: The claim that bells and chimes should be sized according to pitch numbers has no canonical text; only Zheng Xuan stated it on his own authority, and even he called it a hypothetical method.
translations.idiomatic: The notion that bells and chimes should be sized by pitch ratios has no basis in canonical text. Only Zheng Xuan asserted it on his own, and even he admitted it was hypothetical.

sentences.zh: 孔穎達作疏，因而述之。

translations.literal: Kong Yingda wrote a commentary and repeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda followed him in his commentary.

sentences.zh: 據曆代史籍，亦無鍾磬依律數大小之說，其康成、穎達等即非身曾製作樂器。

translations.literal: According to historical records through the ages, there is likewise no tradition of sizing bells and chimes by pitch numbers; men such as Xuan and Yingda never personally made musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Historical records across the dynasties contain no precedent for sizing bells and chimes by pitch ratios, and neither Xuan nor Yingda ever made instruments themselves.

sentences.zh: 至如言‘ 磬前長三律，二尺七寸；

translations.literal: As for the saying that "the front of the chime spans three pitch lengths, two chi seven cun;
translations.idiomatic: As for the rule that "the chime's front spans three pitch-lengths, two chi seven cun;

sentences.zh: 後長二律，一尺八寸，是磬有大小之製’者，據此以黃鍾為律。

translations.literal: the back spans two pitch lengths, one chi eight cun—thus chimes have large and small designs," this takes the Yellow Bell as the pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: the back spans two pitch-lengths, one chi eight cun—so chimes come in graded sizes"—that calculation takes Yellow Bell as the standard pitch.

sentences.zh: 臣曾依此法造黃鍾特磬者，止得林鍾律聲。

translations.literal: When your servant once made a Yellow Bell special stone chime by this method, it produced only the pitch of Forest Bell.
translations.idiomatic: When I once cast a Yellow Bell stone chime by this method, it sounded only Forest Bell.

sentences.zh: 若隨律長短為鍾磬大小之製，則黃鍾長二尺二寸半，減至應鍾，則形製大小比黃鍾才四分之一。

translations.literal: If bells and chimes were sized by the length of each pitch, with the Yellow Bell at two chi two and a half cun and decreasing down to the Ying Bell, the physical form would be only one-quarter that of the Yellow Bell.
