translations.idiomatic: If bells and chimes were scaled to pitch length—Yellow Bell at two chi two and a half cun, tapering down to Ying Bell—the smallest would be only one-quarter the Yellow Bell's size.

sentences.zh: 又九月、十月以無射、應鍾為宮，即黃鍾、大呂反為商聲，宮小而商大，是君弱臣強之象。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the ninth and tenth months Wushe and Ying Bell serve as gong, so Yellow Bell and Great Pipe become shang instead; the tonic small and the shang large—an image of a weak ruler and strong ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the ninth and tenth months, when Wushe and Ying Bell serve as gong, Yellow Bell and Great Pipe become shang—the tonic small and the shang large, an omen of a weak sovereign and powerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 今參酌其鎛鍾、特磬制度，欲且各依律數，算定長短、大小、容受之數，仍以皇祐中黍尺為法，鑄大呂、應鍾鍾磬各一，即見形製、聲韻所歸。”

translations.literal: Now, weighing the regulations for bo bells and special stone chimes, I wish provisionally to calculate length, size, and capacity for each according to pitch numbers, still using the millet-foot standard of the Huangyou era as the rule, and cast one bell and chime each for Great Pipe and Ying Bell, so that the resulting form and pitch may be seen."
translations.idiomatic: I propose, after reviewing the bo-bell and stone-chime regulations, to calculate length, size, and capacity for each pitch, using the Huangyou millet-foot as the standard, and cast one bell and one chime each for Great Pipe and Ying Bell to see where form and pitch actually fall."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 五月，翰林學士承旨王拱辰言：“奉詔詳定大樂，比臣至局，鍾磬已成。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Hanlin Academician Exemplar Wang Gongchen said: "Having received orders to examine and fix the great music, by the time your servant reached the bureau the bells and chimes were already finished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Hanlin Academician Exemplar Wang Gongchen reported: "Ordered to review the great music, I found the bells and chimes already completed when I reached the bureau.

sentences.zh: 竊緣律有長短，磬有大小，黃鍾九寸最長，其氣陽，其象土，其正聲為宮，為諸律之首，蓋君德之象，不可並也。

translations.literal: Privately I reflect that pitch tubes have length and shortness and chimes have large and small sizes; the Yellow Bell at nine cun is the longest, its qi is yang, its emblem is earth, its proper sound is gong, and it is head of all pitches—an image of the ruler's virtue that cannot be equated with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: I note that pitch tubes vary in length and chimes in size. Yellow Bell at nine cun is the longest; its qi is yang, its emblem earth; its proper tone is gong, first among the pitches—the image of royal virtue, not to be made equal with the others.

sentences.zh: 今十二鍾磬，一以黃鍾為率，與古為異。

translations.literal: Now all twelve bells and chimes take the Yellow Bell alone as the standard, which differs from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all twelve bells and chimes are now scaled uniformly from Yellow Bell—a departure from ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 臣等亦嚐詢逸、瑗等，皆言‘依律大小，則聲不能諧。

translations.literal: Your servants also once questioned Yi, Yuan, and the others, and all said, "If sized according to pitch, the sounds cannot harmonize."
translations.idiomatic: We also questioned Yi, Yuan, and the others, who all said, "Size them strictly by pitch and the tones will not harmonize."

sentences.zh: ’故臣竊有疑，請下詳定大樂所，更稽古義參定之。”

translations.literal: Therefore your servant privately has doubts and asks that the matter be sent down to the Bureau for Examining and Fixing the Great Music to investigate ancient meaning and reconsider it."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore have my doubts and ask that the case be referred back to the Bureau for Examining and Fixing the Great Music for a fresh review against ancient principle."

sentences.zh: 是月，知諫院李兌言：“曩者紫宸殿閱太常新樂，議者以鍾之形製未中律度，遂斥而不用，復詔近臣詳定。

translations.literal: That month, Remonstrance Bureau Officer Li Dui said: "Formerly, when the new music of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was reviewed in the Hall of Purple Brightness, commentators held that the bells' design did not match pitch standards, so they were rejected and not used, and attendant ministers were again ordered to examine and fix the matter.
translations.idiomatic: That month Remonstrance Bureau Officer Li Dui said: "When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' new music was reviewed in the Hall of Purple Brightness, critics found the bells out of pitch and rejected them. The court then ordered a fresh review by senior officials.

sentences.zh: 竊聞崇文院聚議，而王拱辰欲更前史之義，王洙不從，議論喧嘖。

translations.literal: I have heard that at the Hall for Venerating Literature they gathered to debate, Wang Gongchen wishing to revise the meaning found in earlier histories while Wang Shu would not follow, and the discussion grew loud and contentious.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that at the Hall for Venerating Literature the debate has grown heated: Wang Gongchen wants to overturn the interpretations of earlier histories, Wang Shu refuses to go along, and the argument has turned noisy.

sentences.zh: 夫樂之道廣大微妙，非知音入神，豈可輕議？

translations.literal: The way of music is vast and subtle; unless one knows sound and enters the spirit of it, how can one discuss it lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Music is vast and subtle. Without true mastery of tone and spirit, who may speak of it lightly?

sentences.zh: 西漢去聖尚近，有制氏世典大樂，但能紀其鏗鏘，而不能言其義。

translations.literal: In Western Han, still close to the sages, the Zhi clan hereditarily kept charge of the great music, yet could only record its clangor and could not explain its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han was still near the sages, and the Zhi clan held hereditary charge of the great music—yet they could record its clangor, not explain its meaning.

sentences.zh: 況今又千餘年，而欲求三代之音，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: How much more now, more than a thousand years later, to seek the sounds of the Three Dynasties—is it not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: After another thousand years and more, is it not folly to expect the music of the Three Dynasties?

sentences.zh: 且阮逸罪廢之人，安能通聖明述作之事？

translations.literal: Moreover, Ruan Yi is a man dismissed for crime—how can he comprehend work of sage clarity and enlightened composition?
translations.idiomatic: And Ruan Yi is a disgraced and dismissed man—what competence has he for work that demands sage clarity?

sentences.zh: 務為異說，欲規恩賞。

translations.literal: He strives for unusual theories, seeking to plot for favor and reward.
translations.idiomatic: He peddles eccentric theories in hope of winning favor and reward.

sentences.zh: 朝廷製樂數年，當國財匱乏之時，煩費甚廣。

translations.literal: The court has been making music for several years, at a time when state finances were depleted, with very great trouble and expense.
translations.idiomatic: The court has spent years on this music at a time of depleted treasury, at enormous trouble and cost.

sentences.zh: 器既成矣，又欲改為，雖命兩府大臣監議，然未能裁定其當。

translations.literal: The instruments are already finished, yet there is again a wish to change them; although the Two Departments' senior ministers were ordered to supervise deliberation, they still cannot decide what is right.
translations.idiomatic: The instruments are finished, yet the court wants to redo them. Even with Two Departments ministers supervising the debate, no one can settle what is right.

sentences.zh: 請以新成鍾磬與祖宗舊樂參校其聲，但取諧和近雅者合用之。”

translations.literal: I ask that the newly finished bells and chimes be compared with the ancestral old music for their sound, and that only what harmonizes and approaches elegance be adopted for joint use.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the new bells and chimes be tested against the ancestral music, and that whatever harmonizes and approaches true elegance be adopted for use."

sentences.zh: 六月，帝御紫宸殿，奏太常新定《大安之樂》，召輔臣至省府、館閣預觀焉，賜詳定官器幣有差。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the emperor attended the Hall of Purple Brightness, and the Court of Ceremonies performed the newly fixed Music of Great Tranquility. He summoned chief ministers to the ministries, agencies, and academies for a preview, and bestowed vessels and ceremonial goods on the examining officials according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor attended the Hall of Purple Brightness, where the Court of Ceremonies performed the newly fixed Music of Great Tranquility. He summoned chief ministers to the ministries, agencies, and academies for a preview and bestowed vessels and ceremonial goods on the examining officials according to rank.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔：“ 南郊姑用舊樂，其新定《大安之樂》，常祀及朝會用之。”

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict said: "For the Southern Suburban sacrifice, the old music is to be used for the time being. The newly fixed Music of Great Tranquility is to be used for regular sacrifices and court assemblies."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict ordered: "For the Southern Suburban sacrifice, use the old music for the time being. The newly fixed Music of Great Tranquility is to be used for regular sacrifices and court assemblies."

sentences.zh: 翰林學士胡宿上言：“自古無並用二樂之理，今舊樂高，新樂下，相去一律，難並用。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Hu Su memorialized: "From antiquity there has never been a principle of using two musics at once. Now the old music is higher and the new music lower — they differ by one pitch standard, and it is hard to use them together.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Hu Su memorialized: "From antiquity there has never been a principle of using two musics at once. The old music is pitched higher and the new music lower — they differ by one standard, and the two cannot be used together.

sentences.zh: 且新樂未施郊廟，先用之朝會，非先王薦上帝、配祖考之意。”

translations.literal: Moreover, the new music has not yet been applied at suburban and temple altars, yet it is first used at court assemblies — this is not the intent of the ancient kings in offering to the Supreme Lord and matching the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the new music has not yet been used at suburban and temple altars, yet it is deployed first at court assemblies. That is not what the ancient kings intended when they offered to the Supreme Lord and paired the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，禦崇政殿，召近臣、宗室、台諫、省府推判官觀新樂並新作晉鼓。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he attended the Hall of Promoting Governance and summoned attendant ministers, members of the imperial clan, remonstrance officials, and acting officials of the ministries and agencies to view the new music and the newly made Jin drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he attended the Hall of Promoting Governance and summoned attendant ministers, members of the imperial clan, remonstrance officials, and acting officials of the ministries and agencies to view the new music and the newly made Jin drums.

sentences.zh: 乃以瑗為大理寺丞，逸復尚書屯田員外郎，保信領榮州防禦使，入內東頭供奉官賈宣吉為內殿承製，並以製鍾律成，特遷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan was made Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Yi was restored as Supernumerary Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue's Colonization Bureau; Baoxin was appointed Defender-in-Chief of Rong Prefecture; and Palace Attendant of the Eastern Inner Gate Jia Xuanji was made Palace Draftsman — all specially promoted for completing the manufacture of bells and pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was then made Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Yi was restored as Supernumerary Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue's Colonization Bureau; Baoxin was appointed Defender-in-Chief of Rong Prefecture; and Palace Attendant of the Eastern Inner Gate Jia Xuanji was made Palace Draftsman — all specially promoted for completing the bells and pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，言者多以陰陽不和由大樂未定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, many commentators held that yin and yang were out of harmony because the great music had not been fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 1, many commentators blamed the disharmony of yin and yang on the failure to fix the great music.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“樂之不合於古久矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That music has not accorded with antiquity for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Music has failed to accord with antiquity for a long time.

sentences.zh: 水旱之來，係時政得失，豈特樂所召哉？”

translations.literal: When flood and drought come, they depend on the gains and losses of current policy — how could music alone summon them?"
translations.idiomatic: When flood and drought come, they reflect the gains and losses of current policy. How could music alone summon them?"

sentences.zh: 二年，潭州上瀏陽縣所得古鍾，送太常。

translations.literal: In the second year, Tan Prefecture submitted an ancient bell found in Liuyang County, and it was sent to the Court of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Tan Prefecture submitted an ancient bell found in Liuyang County, and it was sent to the Court of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，李照斥王樸樂音高，乃作新樂，下其聲。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zhao had rejected Wang Pu's music as too high in pitch, then made new music and lowered the sound.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Zhao had rejected Wang Pu's music as too high in pitch, composed new music, and lowered the pitch.

sentences.zh: 太常歌工病其太濁，歌不成聲，私賂鑄工，使減銅齊，而聲稍清，歌乃協。

translations.literal: The Court of Ceremonies' singing craftsmen found it too muddy to sing properly. They privately bribed the casting craftsmen to reduce the copper alloy, whereupon the sound grew somewhat clearer and the singing harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Ceremonies' singers found the tone too muddy to sing cleanly. They privately bribed the casters to reduce the copper alloy, the sound grew somewhat clearer, and the singing finally harmonized.

sentences.zh: 然照卒莫之辨。

translations.literal: Yet Zhao never discerned this in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao never discovered it.

sentences.zh: 又樸所製編鍾皆側垂，照、瑗皆非之。

translations.literal: Also, all the chime bells Wang Pu made hung askew; Zhao and Yuan both rejected this.
translations.idiomatic: All the chime bells Wang Pu made also hung askew, and both Zhao and Yuan rejected them.

sentences.zh: 及照將鑄鍾，給銅於鑄瀉務，得古編鍾一，工人不敢毀，乃藏於太常。

translations.literal: When Zhao was about to cast bells, copper was supplied at the casting foundry, and one ancient chime bell was obtained. The craftsmen dared not destroy it, so it was stored in the Court of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was about to cast bells, copper was supplied at the casting foundry and an ancient chime bell turned up. The craftsmen dared not destroy it, so it was kept in the Court of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 鍾不知何代所作，其銘云：“粵朕皇祖寶龢鍾，粵斯萬年，子子孫孫永寶用。”

translations.literal: The bell's age was unknown. Its inscription read: "This is Our August Forebear's treasured harmon bell — may it endure for myriad years; may sons and grandsons forever treasure and use it."
translations.idiomatic: No one knew from which age the bell came. Its inscription read: "This is Our August Forebear's treasured harmon bell — may it endure for myriad years; may sons and grandsons forever treasure and use it."

sentences.zh: 叩其聲，與樸鍾夷則清聲合，而其形側垂。

translations.literal: When struck, its sound matched the clear Yize tone of Wang Pu's bell, yet its form hung askew.
translations.idiomatic: When struck, its tone matched the clear Yize pitch of Wang Pu's bell, yet its form hung askew.

sentences.zh: 瑗後改鑄，正其鈕，使下垂，叩之弇，鬱而不揚。

translations.literal: Later Yuan recast it, straightened the suspension loop so it hung downward, but when struck it was muffled — dull and not resonant.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan recast it, straightened the suspension loop so it hung straight down, but when struck it was muffled — dull and without resonance.

sentences.zh: 其鎛鍾又長甬而震掉，聲不和。

translations.literal: His set bells also had long stems and shook loose; the sound did not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: His set bells also had long stems and shook loose, and their tones did not harmonize.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎劉羲叟謂人曰：“此與周景王無射鍾無異，上將有眩惑之疾。”

translations.literal: Assistant Editorial Director Liu Xisou told others: "This is no different from King Jing of Zhou's Wushe bell; the sovereign will suffer from dizziness and confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Editorial Director Liu Xisou told others: "This is no different from King Jing of Zhou's Wushe bell. The sovereign will suffer dizziness and confusion."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年正月，帝御大慶殿受朝，前一夕，殿庭設仗衛、既具而大雨雪，至壓宮架折，帝於禁中跣而告天，遂暴感風眩，人以羲叟之言為驗。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Jiayou, the emperor attended court reception at the Hall of Great Celebration. The night before, armed guards were arrayed in the courtyard; once all was ready, heavy rain and snow fell until the palace musical frame was crushed and broken. The emperor, barefoot in the inner palace, prayed to Heaven, and suddenly took a violent chill with dizziness — people took Liu Xisou's words as fulfilled prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiayou 1 the emperor received court at the Hall of Great Celebration. The night before, armed guards had been arrayed in the courtyard; once all was ready, heavy rain and snow fell until the palace musical frame was crushed and broken. The emperor, barefoot in the inner palace, prayed to Heaven and suddenly took a violent chill with dizziness. People took Liu Xisou's words as prophecy fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 八月，御製恭謝樂章。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the emperor composed thanksgiving hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor composed thanksgiving hymn texts.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔恭謝用舊樂。

translations.literal: That month, an edict ordered that the thanksgiving rite use the old music.
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict ordered the thanksgiving rite to use the old music.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，御製祫享樂舞名：僖祖奏《大基》，順祖奏《大祚》，翼祖奏《大熙》，宣祖奏《大光》，太祖奏《大統》，太宗奏《大昌》，真宗奏《大治》，孝惠皇后奏《淑安》，孝章皇后奏《靜安》，淑德皇后奏《柔安》，章懷皇后奏《和安》，迎神、送神奏《懷安》，皇帝升降奏《肅安》，奠瓚奏《顧安》，奉俎、徹豆奏《充安》，飲福奏《禧安》，亞獻、終獻奏《祐安》，退文舞、迎武舞奏《顯安》，皇帝歸大次奏《定安》，登樓禮成奏《聖安》，駕回奏《采茨》；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, the emperor fixed the names of music and dance for the joint spirit feast: for Emperor Xi-zu, "Great Foundation"; for Emperor Shun-zu, "Great Fortune"; for Emperor Yi-zu, "Great Splendor"; for Emperor Xuan-zu, "Great Radiance"; for Emperor Taizu, "Great Succession"; for Emperor Taizong, "Great Flourishing"; for Emperor Zhenzong, "Great Order"; for Empress Xiaohui, "Shu An"; for Empress Xiaozhang, "Jing An"; for Empress Shude, "Rou An"; for Empress Zhanghuai, "He An"; for welcoming and escorting the spirits, "Huai An"; for the emperor's ascent and descent, "Su An"; for laying the libation cup, "Gu An"; for presenting the sacrificial meat and removing the dishes, "Chong An"; for drinking the blessing, "Xi An"; for the secondary and final offerings, "You An"; for retiring the civil dance and welcoming the martial dance, "Xian An"; for the emperor's return to the side hall, "Ding An"; for completion of the tower rite, "Sheng An"; for the imperial carriage's return, "Cai Ci";
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year the emperor fixed the names of music and dance for the joint spirit feast: for Emperor Xi-zu, "Great Foundation"; for Emperor Shun-zu, "Great Fortune"; for Emperor Yi-zu, "Great Splendor"; for Emperor Xuan-zu, "Great Radiance"; for Emperor Taizu, "Great Succession"; for Emperor Taizong, "Great Flourishing"; for Emperor Zhenzong, "Great Order"; for Empress Xiaohui, "Shu An"; for Empress Xiaozhang, "Jing An"; for Empress Shude, "Rou An"; for Empress Zhanghuai, "He An"; for welcoming and escorting the spirits, "Huai An"; for the emperor's ascent and descent, "Su An"; for laying the libation cup, "Gu An"; for presenting the sacrificial meat and removing the dishes, "Chong An"; for drinking the blessing, "Xi An"; for the secondary and final offerings, "You An"; for retiring the civil dance and welcoming the martial dance, "Xian An"; for the emperor's return to the side hall, "Ding An"; for completion of the tower rite, "Sheng An"; for the imperial carriage's return, "Cai Ci";

sentences.zh: 文舞曰《化成治定》，武舞曰《崇功昭德》。

translations.literal: The civil dance was called "Transforming into Order and Settling Governance"; the martial dance was called "Honoring Merit and Proclaiming Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance was called "Transforming into Order and Settling Governance"; the martial dance was called "Honoring Merit and Proclaiming Virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝自製迎神、送神樂章，詔宰臣富弼等撰《大祚》至《采茨》曲詞十八。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed the hymn texts for welcoming and escorting the spirits, and ordered Chief Minister Fu Bi and others to write the lyrics for eighteen pieces from "Great Fortune" through "Cai Ci."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself composed the hymn texts for welcoming and escorting the spirits and ordered Chief Minister Fu Bi and others to write the lyrics for eighteen pieces from "Great Fortune" through "Cai Ci."

sentences.zh: 七年八月，御製明堂迎神樂章，皆肄於太常。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, the emperor composed Bright Hall hymn texts for welcoming the spirits; all were rehearsed at the Court of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year the emperor composed Bright Hall hymn texts for welcoming the spirits, and all were rehearsed at the Court of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王珪言：“昔之作樂，以五聲播於八音，調和諧合而與治道通，先王用於天地、宗廟、社稷，事於山川鬼神，使鳥獸盡感，況於人乎？

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui said: "In ancient times music was made by spreading the five tones through the eight kinds of sound, harmonizing and uniting so as to connect with the way of governance. The former kings used it for Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; they served mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits, so that birds and beasts were fully moved — how much more so men?
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui said: "In ancient times music spread the five tones through the eight kinds of sound, harmonizing them so as to connect with the way of governance. The former kings used it for Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; they served mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits, moving birds and beasts to the full — how much more so men?

sentences.zh: 然則樂雖盛而音虧，未知其所以為樂也。

translations.literal: Yet if music is grand but its tones are deficient, one does not know what music is for.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if music is grand but its tones are deficient, one no longer knows what music is for.

sentences.zh: 今郊廟升歌之樂，有金、石、絲、竹、匏、土、革而無木音。

translations.literal: Now in the ascending hymn music at suburban and temple altars, there are metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, clay, and hide — but no wood tone.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ascending hymn music at suburban and temple altars has metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, clay, and hide — but no wood tone.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂敔者，聖人用以著樂之始終，顧豈容有缺耶？

translations.literal: The so-called yi — the wooden clapper the sages used to mark the beginning and end of music — surely it cannot be allowed to be missing?
translations.idiomatic: The yi — the wooden clapper the sages used to mark the beginning and end of music — surely cannot be omitted?

sentences.zh: 且樂莫隆於《韶》，《書》曰‘戛擊’，是、之用。

translations.literal: Moreover, no music is loftier than the "Shao." The Documents says "strike the yi" — the yi is used for this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no music is loftier than the "Shao." The Documents says "strike the yi" — the yi is what is used.

sentences.zh: 既雲下而擊鞀，知鳴球與敔之在堂，故《傳》曰：‘堂上堂下，各有敔也’。

translations.literal: Since it also says "strike the to below," we know that sounding spheres and the yi are in the hall. Hence the Commentary says: "In the upper hall and lower hall, each has its yi."
translations.idiomatic: Since it also says "strike the to below," we know that sounding spheres and the yi belong in the hall. Hence the Commentary says: "In the upper hall and lower hall, each has its yi."

sentences.zh: 今陛下躬祠明堂，宜詔有司考樂之失而合八音之和。”

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty personally sacrifices at the Bright Hall; you should order the responsible officials to examine faults in the music and restore the harmony of the eight kinds of sound."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty personally sacrifices at the Bright Hall, you should order the responsible officials to examine faults in the music and restore the harmony of the eight kinds of sound."

sentences.zh: 於是下禮官議，而堂上始置敔。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was sent down to the ceremonial officials for deliberation, and a yi was first placed in the upper hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the matter was sent down to the ceremonial officials for deliberation, and a yi was placed in the upper hall for the first time.

sentences.zh: 又秘閣校理裴煜奏：“大祠與國忌同者，有司援舊制，禮樂備而不作。

translations.literal: Also Editorial Director of the Secretariat Pavilion Pei Yu memorialized: "When a major sacrifice falls on the same day as a state mourning anniversary, the responsible officials cite the old rule: rites and music are prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial Director of the Secretariat Pavilion Pei Yu also memorialized: "When a major sacrifice falls on the same day as a state mourning anniversary, the responsible officials cite the old rule: rites and music are prepared but not performed.

sentences.zh: 忌日必哀，誌有所至，其不有樂，宜也。

translations.literal: On a mourning anniversary one must grieve — the will has its reach; that there should be no music is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: On a mourning anniversary one must grieve; the heart has its proper limit, and to omit music then is fitting.

sentences.zh: 然樂所以降格神祇非以適一己之私也。

translations.literal: Yet music is what brings down and summons the spirits — it is not to gratify one's private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet music is what brings down and summons the spirits; it is not meant to gratify private feeling.

sentences.zh: 謹案開元中禮部建言，忌日享廟應用樂。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that in the Kaiyuan era the Ministry of Rites proposed that on mourning anniversaries, temple offerings should use music.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that in the Kaiyuan era the Ministry of Rites proposed that temple offerings on mourning anniversaries should use music.

sentences.zh: 裴寬立議，廟尊忌卑則作樂，廟卑忌尊則備而不奏。

translations.literal: Pei Kuan established the rule: if the temple is higher in rank and the mourning anniversary lower, perform music; if the temple is lower and the mourning anniversary higher, prepare but do not play.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan established the rule: if the temple outranks the mourning anniversary, perform music; if the mourning anniversary outranks the temple, prepare the music but do not play it.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說以寬議為是。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue held Pei Kuan's proposal correct.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue held Pei Kuan's proposal to be correct.

sentences.zh: 宗廟如此，則天地、日月、社稷之祠用樂明矣。

translations.literal: If this is so for the ancestral temple, then the use of music in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, and the altars of soil and grain is clear.
translations.idiomatic: If this holds for the ancestral temple, then the use of music in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, and the altars of soil and grain is clear.

sentences.zh: 臣以為凡大祠天地、日月、社稷與忌日同者，伏請用樂，其在廟則如寬之議。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that whenever major sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, or the altars of soil and grain fall on the same day as a mourning anniversary, music should be used; as for temples, follow Pei Kuan's rule.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that whenever major sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, or the altars of soil and grain fall on the same day as a mourning anniversary, music should be used; in temple rites, follow Pei Kuan's rule.

sentences.zh: 所冀略輕存重，不失其稱。”

translations.literal: What is hoped for is to set aside the lesser and preserve the greater, without losing what is proper to each."
translations.idiomatic: What is hoped for is to set aside the lesser and preserve the greater, without losing what is proper to each rank."

sentences.zh: 下其章禮官，議曰“《傳》稱祭天以禋為歆神之始，以血為陳饌之始；

translations.literal: His memorial was sent down to the ceremonial officials, who deliberated and said: "The Commentary states that in sacrificing to Heaven, burning incense is the beginning of delighting the spirit, and presenting blood is the beginning of setting out the offerings;
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was sent down to the ceremonial officials, who deliberated and said: "The Commentary states that in sacrificing to Heaven, burning incense is the beginning of delighting the spirit, and presenting blood is the beginning of setting out the offerings;

sentences.zh: 祭地以埋為歆神之始，以血為陳饌之始。

translations.literal: In sacrificing to Earth, burying is the beginning of delighting the spirit, and presenting blood is the beginning of setting out the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In sacrificing to Earth, burying is the beginning of delighting the spirit, and presenting blood is the beginning of setting out the offerings.

sentences.zh: 宗廟以灌為歆神之始，以腥為陳饒之始。

translations.literal: In the ancestral temple, libation is the beginning of delighting the spirit, and presenting raw meat is the beginning of setting out the sacrificial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple, libation is the beginning of delighting the spirit, and presenting raw meat is the beginning of setting out the sacrificial gifts.

sentences.zh: 然則天地、宗廟皆以樂為致神之始，故曰大祭有三始，謂此也。

translations.literal: Thus for Heaven-and-Earth and the ancestral temple alike, music is the beginning of bringing the spirit down — hence it is said that great sacrifices have three beginnings; this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for Heaven-and-Earth and the ancestral temple alike, music is the beginning of bringing the spirit down. Hence it is said that great sacrifices have three beginnings — this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 天地之間虛豁而不見其形者，陽也。

translations.literal: That which is empty and open between Heaven and Earth and cannot be seen in form is yang.
translations.idiomatic: What is empty and unobstructed between Heaven and Earth, invisible to the eye—that is yang.

sentences.zh: 鬼神居天地之間，不可以人道接也。

translations.literal: Ghosts and spirits dwell between Heaven and Earth; they cannot be approached by human ways.
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts and spirits inhabit the realm between Heaven and Earth and cannot be reached by ordinary human means.

sentences.zh: 聲屬於陽，故樂之音聲號呼召於天地之間，庶幾神明聞之，因而來格，故祭必求諸陽。

translations.literal: Sound belongs to yang; therefore music's tones and voices call out between Heaven and Earth, so that perhaps the spirits will hear and thereby descend; thus in sacrifice one must seek by yang.
translations.idiomatic: Sound belongs to yang. Music's tones and voices therefore cry out between Heaven and Earth, in hope that the spirits will hear and descend in response. Sacrifice must therefore begin by appealing to yang.

sentences.zh: 商人之祭，先奏樂以求神，先求於陽也；

translations.literal: In the sacrifices of the Shang people, music was played first to seek the spirits — seeking yang first;
translations.idiomatic: In Shang ritual, music was performed first to summon the spirits—a priority of yang;

sentences.zh: 次灌地求神於陰，達於淵泉也。

translations.literal: Next, libation was poured on the ground to seek the spirits in yin, reaching to the deep springs.
translations.idiomatic: Next came libation poured on the ground to seek the spirits in yin, reaching down to the deep springs.

sentences.zh: 周人尚臭，四時之祭，先灌地以求神，先求諸陰也。

translations.literal: The Zhou people valued aroma; in the four seasonal sacrifices, libation on the ground was performed first to seek the spirits — seeking yin first.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou people prized fragrant offerings. In their four seasonal sacrifices, libation on the ground came first—to seek the spirits through yin.

sentences.zh: 然則天神、地祇、人鬼之祀不可去樂明矣。

translations.literal: Thus it is clear that sacrifices to the spirits of Heaven, the spirits of Earth, and human ghosts cannot dispense with music.
translations.idiomatic: It is therefore plain that sacrifices to the Heavenly spirits, Earthly spirits, and ancestral ghosts alike cannot do without music.

sentences.zh: 今七廟連室，難分廟忌之尊卑，欲依唐製及國朝故事：廟祭與忌同日，並縣而不作；

translations.literal: Now the seven ancestral temples are connected chambers, making it difficult to distinguish high and low among temple anniversaries; it is desired to follow Tang practice and our dynasty's precedent: when temple sacrifice and death anniversary fall on the same day, suspend bells without performing music;
translations.idiomatic: The seven ancestral temples now share connected halls, making it hard to distinguish precedence among temple anniversaries. We propose to follow Tang practice and our dynasty's established precedent: when a temple sacrifice and a death anniversary fall on the same day, suspend the bells and perform no music;

sentences.zh: 其與別廟諸後忌同者，作之；

translations.literal: When it coincides with the death anniversaries of empresses at separate shrines, perform music;
translations.idiomatic: but when the date coincides with a separate-shrine anniversary of an empress, music should be performed;

sentences.zh: 若祠天地、日月、九宮、太一及蠟百神，並請作樂；

translations.literal: For sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Sun and Moon, the Nine Palaces, Grand Unity, and the year-end rite to the hundred spirits, music is requested for all;
translations.idiomatic: for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Sun and Moon, the Nine Palaces, Grand Unity, and the year-end rite to the hundred spirits, music should be performed in every case;

sentences.zh: 社稷以下諸祠既卑於廟，則樂可不作。”

translations.literal: Since the various sacrifices below the state altars are inferior in rank to the ancestral temple, music need not be performed."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices of lower rank than the ancestral temple, such as those at the state altars, need not include music."

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王珪等以為：“社稷，國之所尊，其祠日若與別廟諸後忌同者，伏請亦不去樂。”

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others stated: "The state altars are among what the state most honors. When their sacrifice day coincides with a separate-shrine anniversary of an empress, we respectfully ask that music likewise not be omitted."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others argued: "The state altars are among what the state most honors. When their sacrifice day coincides with a separate-shrine anniversary of an empress, we respectfully ask that music not be omitted either."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 英宗治平元年六月，太常寺奏，仁宗配饗明堂，奠幣歌《誠安》，酌獻歌《德安》。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhiping, during Emperor Yingzong's reign, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported that at Emperor Renzong's paired enshrinement at the Bright Hall, the silk-offering hymn was Cheng'an and the libation hymn was De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhiping 1, during Emperor Yingzong's reign, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported that at Emperor Renzong's paired enshrinement at the Bright Hall, the silk-offering hymn was "Cheng'an" and the libation hymn was "De'an."

sentences.zh: 二年九月，禮官李育上言：“南郊、太廟二舞郎總六十八，文舞罷，舍羽籥，執幹戚，就為武舞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, ritual official Li Yu memorialized: "At the Southern Suburb and Imperial Ancestral Temple, the two dance officers total sixty-eight. When the civil dance ends, they discard feather and flute, take up shield and axe, and become the military dance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year, ritual official Li Yu memorialized: "At the Southern Suburb and Imperial Ancestral Temple, the two dance officers total sixty-eight. When the civil dance ends, they discard feather and flute, take up shield and axe, and become the military dance.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按舊典，文、武二舞各用八佾，凡祀圜丘、祀宗廟，太樂令率工人以入，就位，文舞入，陳於架北，武舞立於架南。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes the old canon: civil and military dances each employ eight rows of dancers. Whenever sacrificing at the Round Altar or the ancestral temple, the Director of Grand Music leads the musicians in; once in position, the civil dancers enter and array themselves north of the frame, and the military dancers stand south of the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully notes the old canon: civil and military dances each employ eight rows of dancers. Whenever sacrificing at the Round Altar or the ancestral temple, the Director of Grand Music leads the musicians in; once in position, the civil dancers enter and array themselves north of the frame, and the military dancers stand south of the frame.

sentences.zh: 又文舞出，武舞入，有送迎之曲，名曰《舒和》，亦曰《同和》，凡三十一章，止用一曲。

translations.literal: Further, when the civil dancers withdraw and the military dancers enter, there is a welcoming and escorting piece called "Shuhe," also called "Tonghe"; though there are thirty-one chapters in all, only one melody is used.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil dancers withdraw and the military dancers enter, there is a welcoming and escorting piece called "Shuhe," also called "Tonghe." Though there are thirty-one chapters in all, only one melody is used.

sentences.zh: 是進退同時，行綴先定，步武容體，各應樂節。

translations.literal: Thus advance and retreat occur simultaneously, the ranks and positions are set beforehand, and steps, bearing, and form each accord with the musical beats.
translations.idiomatic: Advance and retreat were simultaneous, ranks and positions fixed in advance, and steps, bearing, and form each matched the musical beats.

sentences.zh: 夫《玄德升聞之舞》象揖讓，《天下大定之舞》象征伐，柔毅舒急不侔，而所法所習亦異，不當中易也。

translations.literal: The Dance of Mystic Virtue Ascending to Heaven represents yielding and deference; the Dance of Great Peace Under Heaven represents conquest and battle. Softness and firmness, ease and urgency are not alike, and what they embody and what dancers are trained in also differ — they should not be swapped midway.
translations.idiomatic: The Dance of Mystic Virtue Ascending to Heaven represents yielding and deference; the Dance of Great Peace Under Heaven represents conquest and battle. Softness and firmness, ease and urgency are not alike, and what they embody and what dancers are trained in also differ—they should not be swapped midway.

sentences.zh: 竊惟天神皆降，地祇皆出，八音克諧，祖考來格，天子親執珪幣，‘相維辟公’，‘嚴恭寅畏’，可謂極矣。

translations.literal: I reflect that the spirits of Heaven all descend, the spirits of Earth all emerge, the eight categories of sound achieve harmony, and the ancestors arrive; the Son of Heaven personally holds jade and silk — "The ministers assist, O Lord"; "solemn, reverent, diligent, and fearful" — one could scarcely go further.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the occasion: the spirits of Heaven descend, the spirits of Earth emerge, the eight categories of sound fall into harmony, and the ancestors arrive. The Son of Heaven personally holds jade and silk—"The ministers assist, O Lord"; "solemn, reverent, diligent, and fearful." The ritual could scarcely be carried further.

sentences.zh: 而舞者紛然縱橫於下，進退取舍，蹙迫如是，豈明有德、象有功之誼哉？

translations.literal: Yet below, the dancers rush about in every direction, advancing, retreating, choosing, and discarding in such cramped fashion — how does this express virtue made clear and merit made manifest?
translations.idiomatic: Yet below, the dancers rush about in every direction, advancing, retreating, choosing, and discarding in such cramped fashion—how does this express virtue made clear and merit made manifest?

sentences.zh: 國家三年而躬一郊，同殿而享八室，而舞者闕如，名曰二舞，實一舞也。

translations.literal: The state performs the suburban sacrifice personally once every three years, serving eight chambers in one hall, yet the dancers are insufficient in number — they are called two dances but are in fact one dance.
translations.idiomatic: The state performs the suburban sacrifice in person once every three years, serving eight chambers in one hall, yet the dancers are insufficient in number—they are called two dances but are in fact one dance.

sentences.zh: 且如大朝會所以宴臣下，而舞者備其數；

translations.literal: Moreover, at great court assemblies meant to feast the ministers below, the dancers are fully manned;
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies meant to feast the ministers below, the dancers are fully manned;

sentences.zh: 郊廟所以事天地、祖考，而舞者減其半：殊未為稱。

translations.literal: Yet at suburban and temple rites meant to serve Heaven and Earth and the ancestors, the dancers are cut by half — this is hardly fitting.
translations.idiomatic: yet at suburban and temple rites meant to serve Heaven and Earth and the ancestors, the dancers are cut by half—this is hardly fitting.

sentences.zh: 事有近而不可邇，禮有繁而不可省，所係者大，而有司之職不敢廢也。

translations.literal: Some matters seem close at hand yet must not be approached lightly; some rites seem elaborate yet must not be simplified. What is at stake is great, and the officials in charge dare not neglect their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Some matters seem close at hand yet must not be approached lightly; some rites seem elaborate yet must not be simplified. What is at stake is great, and the officials in charge dare not neglect their duty.

sentences.zh: 伏請南郊、太廟文武二舞各用六十四人，以備帝王之禮樂，以明祖宗之功德。”

translations.literal: We respectfully ask that at the Southern Suburb and Imperial Ancestral Temple the civil and military dances each employ sixty-four dancers, to complete the ritual music befitting an emperor, and to manifest the merit and virtue of the ancestral house."
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully ask that at the Southern Suburb and Imperial Ancestral Temple the civil and military dances each employ sixty-four dancers, to complete the ritual music befitting an emperor and to manifest the merit and virtue of the ancestral house."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，學士院建言：“國朝宗廟之樂，各以功德名舞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, the Academy of Hanlin Scholars proposed: "Our dynasty's ancestral temple music names each dance after merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year, the Academy of Hanlin Scholars proposed: "Our dynasty's ancestral temple music names each dance after merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 洪惟英宗，繼天遵業，欽明勤儉，不自暇逸。

translations.literal: Great indeed was Emperor Yingzong, who succeeded Heaven's mandate and followed the inherited enterprise, reverent, clear-sighted, diligent, and frugal, never granting himself leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Great indeed was Emperor Yingzong, who succeeded Heaven's mandate and followed the inherited enterprise—reverent, clear-sighted, diligent, and frugal, never granting himself leisure.

sentences.zh: 踐祚未幾，而恩行威立，固已超軼百王之上。

translations.literal: He had not long ascended the throne before kindness was practiced and authority established, already surpassing the hundred kings of old.
translations.idiomatic: He had not long ascended the throne before kindness was practiced and authority established, already surpassing the hundred kings of old.

sentences.zh: 今厚陵復土，祔廟有期，而樂名未立，亡以詔萬世。

translations.literal: Now work on the thick mound has been completed and enshrinement in the ancestral temple is at hand, yet no dance name has been established — there is no means to proclaim this to ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Work on the thick mound has now been completed and enshrinement in the ancestral temple is at hand, yet no dance name has been established—there is no means to proclaim this to ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 請上樂章及名廟所用舞曰《大英》之舞。

translations.literal: We ask that musical movements be submitted and that the dance used at the temple be named the Dance of Great Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that musical movements be submitted and that the dance used at the temple be named the Dance of Great Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 自後禮官、御史有所建明，而詳定朝會及郊廟禮文官於樂節有議論，率以時考正之。”

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever ritual officials or censorial officials made proposals, and officers who fixed court assembly and suburban-temple ritual texts raised questions about musical procedure, these were generally examined and corrected in a timely manner."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever ritual officials or censorial officials made proposals, and the officers who fixed court assembly and suburban-temple ritual texts raised questions about musical procedure, these were generally examined and corrected in a timely manner."

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧九年，禮官以宗廟樂節而有請者三：

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining, during Emperor Shenzong's reign, ritual officials made three requests regarding ancestral temple musical procedure:
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 9, during Emperor Shenzong's reign, ritual officials made three requests regarding ancestral temple musical procedure:

sentences.zh: 其一、今祠太廟《興安之曲》，舉而聲已過，舉而聲不止，則始終之節未明。

translations.literal: First: in the present ancestral temple rite, for the melody "Xing'an," sometimes the clapper is raised after the sound has already ended, and sometimes while the sound still continues — thus the beginning and ending beats are unclear.
translations.idiomatic: First: in the present ancestral temple rite, for the melody "Xing'an," sometimes the clapper is raised after the sound has already ended, and sometimes while the sound still continues—thus the beginning and ending beats are unclear.

sentences.zh: 請祠祭用樂，一奏將終，則戛而聲少止，擊則樂復作，以盡合止之義。

translations.literal: We ask that when music is used in temple sacrifice, as each movement nears its end, the clapper should strike and the sound briefly cease; then with another strike the music resumes — to fulfill the meaning of ending together.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that when music is used in temple sacrifice, as each movement nears its end, the clapper should strike and the sound briefly cease; then with another strike the music should resume—to fulfill the meaning of harmonized cessation.

sentences.zh: 其二、大樂降神之樂，均聲未齊，短長不協，故舞行疾徐亦不能一。

translations.literal: Second: in the great music for descending spirits, the balanced tones are not uniform and long and short do not accord; therefore the pace of the dance likewise cannot be uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Second: in the great music for descending spirits, the balanced tones are not uniform and long and short do not accord; therefore the pace of the dance likewise cannot be uniform.

sentences.zh: 請以一曲為一變，六變用六，九變用九，則樂舞始終莫不應節。

translations.literal: We ask that one melody serve as one change: six changes use six melodies, nine changes use nine — then music and dance from beginning to end will none fail to match the beats.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that one melody serve as one change: six changes use six melodies, nine changes use nine—then music and dance from beginning to end will none fail to match the beats.

sentences.zh: 其三、周人尚臭，蓋先灌而後作樂；

translations.literal: Third: the Zhou people prized fragrant offerings; they generally poured libation first and then performed music;
translations.idiomatic: Third: the Zhou people prized fragrant offerings; they generally poured libation first and then performed music;

sentences.zh: 本朝宗廟之禮多從周，請先灌而後作樂。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's ancestral temple rites largely follow the Zhou; we ask to pour libation first and then perform music.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's ancestral temple rites largely follow the Zhou; we ask to pour libation first and then perform music.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，詳定所以朝會樂而有請者十：

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the office for fixing court assembly music made ten requests:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the office for fixing court assembly music made ten requests:

sentences.zh: 其一、唐元正、冬至大朝會，迎送王公用《舒和》，《開元禮》以初入門《舒和之樂》作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: First: at Tang New Year's and winter solstice great court assemblies, welcoming and escorting princes and dukes used "Shuhe." The Kaiyuan Rites prescribed that upon first entering the gate, the Music of Shuhe should begin; upon reaching one's position, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: First: at Tang New Year's and winter solstice great court assemblies, welcoming and escorting princes and dukes used "Shuhe." The Kaiyuan Rites prescribed that upon first entering the gate, the Music of Shuhe should begin; upon reaching one's position, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 蓋作樂所以待王公，今中書、門下、親王、使相先於丹墀上東西立，皇帝升御坐，乃奏樂引三品以上官，未為得禮。

translations.literal: Music was performed to receive princes and dukes. Now the Central Secretariat, Chancellery, imperial princes, and frontier commissioners stand east and west on the red steps before the emperor ascends the throne; only then is music played to lead in officials of third rank and above — this is not proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Music was performed to receive princes and dukes. Now the Central Secretariat, Chancellery, imperial princes, and frontier commissioners stand east and west on the red steps before the emperor ascends the throne; only then is music played to lead in officials of third rank and above—this is not proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 請侍從及應赴官先就立位，中書、門下、親王、使相、諸司三品、尚書省四品及宗室、將軍以上，班分東西入，《正安之樂》作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: We ask that attendants and officials required to attend take their positions first; then the Central Secretariat, Chancellery, imperial princes, frontier commissioners, department heads of third rank, fourth-rank officials of the Department of State Affairs, and imperial clansmen and generals and above should enter in east-west ranks while the Music of Zheng'an is performed; upon reaching position, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that attendants and officials required to attend take their positions first; then the Central Secretariat, Chancellery, imperial princes, frontier commissioners, department heads of third rank, fourth-rank officials of the Department of State Affairs, and imperial clansmen and generals and above should enter in east-west ranks while the Music of Zheng'an is performed; upon reaching position, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 其二、今朝會儀：舉第一爵，宮縣奏《和安之曲》，第二、第三、第四，登歌作《慶雲》、《嘉禾》、《靈芝之曲》。

translations.literal: Second: under present court assembly rites, at the first cup the palace ensemble plays "He'an"; at the second, third, and fourth cups, ascent singing performs "Qingyun," "Jiahe," and "Lingzhi."
translations.idiomatic: Second: under present court assembly rites, at the first cup the palace ensemble plays "He'an"; at the second, third, and fourth cups, ascent singing performs "Qingyun," "Jiahe," and "Lingzhi."

sentences.zh: 則是合樂在前、登歌在後，有違古義。

translations.literal: Thus the ensemble music comes first and ascent singing comes after — contrary to ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ensemble music comes first and ascent singing comes after—contrary to ancient meaning.

sentences.zh: 請第一爵，登歌奏《和安之曲》，堂上之樂隨歌而發；

translations.literal: We ask that at the first cup, ascent singing perform "He'an," with the hall music following the song;
translations.idiomatic: We ask that at the first cup, ascent singing perform "He'an," with the hall music following the song;

sentences.zh: 第二爵，笙入奏《慶雲》之曲，止吹笙，餘樂不作；

translations.literal: At the second cup, sheng enter and perform "Qingyun," playing only the sheng while the remaining music is not performed;
translations.idiomatic: at the second cup, sheng enter and perform "Qingyun," playing only the sheng while the remaining music is not performed;

sentences.zh: 第三爵，堂上歌《嘉禾之曲》，堂下吹笙，《瑞木成文之曲》，一歌一吹相間；

translations.literal: At the third cup, the hall sings "Jiahe" while below the hall the sheng plays "Ruimu Chengwen," song and sheng alternating;
translations.idiomatic: at the third cup, the hall sings "Jiahe" while below the hall the sheng plays "Ruimu Chengwen," song and sheng alternating;

sentences.zh: 第四爵，合樂奏《靈芝之曲》，堂上下之樂交作。

translations.literal: At the fourth cup, the combined ensemble performs "Lingzhi," with music above and below the hall performing together.
translations.idiomatic: at the fourth cup, the combined ensemble performs "Lingzhi," with music above and below the hall performing together.

sentences.zh: 其三、定文舞、武舞各為四表，表距四步為酂綴，各六十四。

translations.literal: Third: fix the civil and martial dances each at four markers; four paces between markers make one cadence step, sixty-four each.
translations.idiomatic: Third: fix the civil and martial dances each at four markers; four paces between markers make one cadence step, sixty-four each.

sentences.zh: 文舞者服進賢冠，左執籥，右秉翟，分八佾，二工執纛引前，衣冠同之。

translations.literal: Civil dancers wear the advancing-worthies cap, hold the yue flute in the left hand and dai pheasant-feather streamers in the right, divided into eight rows; two workers carry banner canopies to lead ahead, dress and caps the same.
translations.idiomatic: Civil dancers wear the advancing-worthies cap, hold a yue flute in the left hand and dai pheasant-feather streamers in the right, divided into eight rows; two workers carry banner canopies to lead the way, dressed alike.

sentences.zh: 舞者進蹈安徐，進一步則兩兩相顧揖，三步三揖，四步為三辭之容，是為一成。

translations.literal: The dancers advance with calm, measured steps; advancing one step, pairs turn toward each other and bow; three steps, three bows; four steps form the bearing of three declinations—this is one completion.
translations.idiomatic: The dancers advance with calm, measured steps; with each step forward, pairs turn toward each other and bow; three steps, three bows; four steps form the bearing of three declinations—this constitutes one completion.

sentences.zh: 餘成如之。

translations.literal: The remaining completions follow the same pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining completions follow the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 自南第一表至第二表為第一成，至第三表為再成，至北第一表為三成，覆身卻行至第三表為四成，至第二表為五成，復至南第一表為六成，而武舞入。

translations.literal: From the southern first marker to the second marker is the first completion; to the third marker is the second completion; to the northern first marker is the third completion; turning the body and retreating to the third marker is the fourth completion; to the second marker is the fifth completion; returning again to the southern first marker is the sixth completion, and then the martial dance enters.
translations.idiomatic: From the southern first marker to the second is the first completion; to the third is the second; to the northern first is the third; turning about and retreating to the third marker is the fourth; to the second is the fifth; returning once more to the southern first is the sixth, and then the martial dance enters.

sentences.zh: 今文舞所秉翟羽，則集雉尾置於髹漆之柄，求之古製，實無所本。

translations.literal: Now the dai feathers held in civil dance are gathered pheasant tails placed on lacquered handles—searched against ancient regulations, they in fact have no basis in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Today the dai feathers used in civil dance are simply gathered pheasant tails fixed to lacquered handles—when checked against ancient regulations, they have no genuine precedent.

sentences.zh: 聶崇義圖，羽舞所執類羽葆幢，析羽四重，以結綬係於柄，此纛翳之謂也。

translations.literal: In Nie Chongyi's diagram, what the feather dance holds resembles a plume pennant: feathers layered fourfold, tied to the handle with knotted cords—this is what is meant by the banner canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In Nie Chongyi's diagram, the feather dance holds something resembling a plume pennant: feathers layered fourfold and bound to the handle with knotted cords—this is what is meant by the banner canopy.

sentences.zh: 請按圖以翟羽為之。

translations.literal: We ask to follow the diagram and make them of dai feathers.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that they be made of dai feathers according to the diagram.

sentences.zh: 其四、武舞服平巾幘，左執幹，右執戈。

translations.literal: Fourth: martial dancers wear the flat-cloth headwrap, holding a shield in the left hand and a halberd in the right.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: martial dancers wear the flat-cloth headwrap, with a shield in the left hand and a halberd in the right.

sentences.zh: 二工執旌居前；

translations.literal: Two workers carry pennants at the front;
translations.idiomatic: Two workers carry pennants at the front;

sentences.zh: 執鞀、執鐸各二工；

translations.literal: Two workers each for carrying the handheld drum and the bell-clapper;
translations.idiomatic: two workers each carry the handheld drum and the bell-clapper;

sentences.zh: 金錞二，四工舉；

translations.literal: Two bronze chun bells, four workers to raise them;
translations.idiomatic: two bronze chun bells, raised by four workers;

sentences.zh: 二工執鐲、執鐃；

translations.literal: Two workers carry the bronze cymbals and the nao bells;
translations.idiomatic: two workers carry the bronze cymbals and the nao bells;

sentences.zh: 執相在左，執雅在右，亦各二工；

translations.literal: Those carrying the wooden clapper on the left and the ya clapper on the right, also two workers each;
translations.idiomatic: those carrying the wooden clapper on the left and the ya clapper on the right, also two workers each;

sentences.zh: 夾引舞者，衣冠同之。

translations.literal: Flanking and leading the dancers, dress and caps the same.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking and leading the dancers, they are dressed alike.

sentences.zh: 分八佾於南表前，先振鐸以通鼓，乃擊鼓以警戒，舞工聞鼓聲，則各依酂綴總幹正立定位，堂上長歌以詠歎之。

translations.literal: Divide into eight rows before the southern marker; first strike the bell-clapper to signal the drum, then strike the drum as warning; when the dance workers hear the drum, each according to the cadence steps gathers the shields upright and takes position; long song above the hall chants in praise.
translations.idiomatic: They divide into eight rows before the southern marker; first the bell-clapper is struck to signal the drum, then the drum is beaten as a warning; when the dancers hear the drum, each takes position by cadence step with shield held upright; above the hall, the long song chants in praise.

sentences.zh: 於是播鞀以導舞，舞者進步，自南而北，至最南表，以見舞漸。

translations.literal: Then the handheld drum is sounded to lead the dance; the dancers advance step by step from south to north, reaching the southernmost marker, to show the dance gradually unfolding.
translations.idiomatic: Then the handheld drum is sounded to lead the dance; the dancers advance from south to north, reaching the southernmost marker, showing the dance gradually unfold.

sentences.zh: 然後左右夾振鐸，次擊鼓，以金錞和之，以金鐲節之，以相而輔樂，以雅而陔步。

translations.literal: Then left and right together strike the bell-clapper; next strike the drum; the bronze chun harmonizes with it, the bronze cymbals mark the beat, the wooden clapper assists the music, and the ya clapper marks the pacing steps.
translations.idiomatic: Then the bell-clapper is struck on both sides; next the drum is beaten; the bronze chun harmonizes, the bronze cymbals mark the beat, the wooden clapper supports the music, and the ya clapper marks the pacing steps.

sentences.zh: 舞者發揚蹈厲，為猛賁趫速之狀。

translations.literal: The dancers display vigor and tread with martial force, showing the bearing of ferocious charge and swift advance.
translations.idiomatic: The dancers display vigor and tread with martial force, embodying ferocious charge and swift advance.

sentences.zh: 每步一進，則兩兩以戈盾相向，一擊一刺為一伐，四伐為一成，成謂之變。

translations.literal: With each step forward, pairs face each other with halberd and shield; one strike and one thrust make one battalion action; four battalion actions make one completion; a completion is called a change.
translations.idiomatic: With each step forward, pairs face each other with halberd and shield; one strike and one thrust constitute one battalion action; four such actions make one completion, and each completion is called a change.

sentences.zh: 至第二表為一變；

translations.literal: Reaching the second marker is the first change;
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the second marker is the first change;

sentences.zh: 至第三表為二變；

translations.literal: Reaching the third marker is the second change;
translations.idiomatic: reaching the third marker is the second change;

sentences.zh: 至北第一表為三變；

translations.literal: Reaching the northern first marker is the third change;
translations.idiomatic: reaching the northern first marker is the third change;

sentences.zh: 舞者覆身向堂，卻行而南，至第三表為四變；

translations.literal: The dancers turn toward the hall and retreat southward; reaching the third marker is the fourth change;
translations.idiomatic: the dancers turn toward the hall and retreat southward; reaching the third marker is the fourth change;

sentences.zh: 乃擊刺而前，至第二表回易行列，舂、雅節步分左右而跪，以右膝至地，左足仰起，象以文止武為五變；

translations.literal: Then strike and thrust forward; reaching the second marker, turn and rearrange ranks; the xiang and ya mark the steps as left and right kneel separately—right knee to the ground, left foot raised up—symbolizing restraining martial force with civil refinement as the fifth change;
translations.idiomatic: then they strike and thrust forward; reaching the second marker, they turn and rearrange ranks; the xiang and ya mark the steps as left and right kneel separately—right knee to the ground, left foot raised—symbolizing the restraint of martial force by civil refinement as the fifth change;

sentences.zh: 舞蹈而進，為兵還振旅之狀，振鐸、搖鞀、擊鼓，和以金錞，廢鐲鳴鐃，復至南第一表為六變而舞畢。

translations.literal: Dancing as they advance, showing the bearing of troops returning and regrouping; striking the bell-clapper, shaking the handheld drum, beating the drum, harmonizing with the bronze chun, setting aside the cymbals and sounding the nao bells; returning again to the southern first marker as the sixth change, and the dance is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Dancing as they advance, they show troops returning and regrouping; the bell-clapper is struck, the handheld drum shaken, the drum beaten, the bronze chun harmonized, the cymbals set aside and the nao bells sounded; returning once more to the southern first marker as the sixth change, the dance is complete.

sentences.zh: 古者，人君自舞《大武》，故服冕執幹戚。

translations.literal: In antiquity, the ruler himself danced "Dawu," and therefore wore the ceremonial cap and held shield and axe.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the ruler himself danced "Dawu," and therefore wore the ceremonial cap and held shield and axe.

sentences.zh: 若用八佾而為擊刺之容，則舞者執幹戈。

translations.literal: If using eight rows to perform striking and thrusting movements, then the dancers hold shield and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: If eight rows are used to perform striking and thrusting movements, the dancers should hold shield and halberd.

sentences.zh: 說者謂武舞戰象樂六奏，每一奏之中，率以戈矛四擊刺。

translations.literal: Expositors say the martial dance is the martial image in music's six performances; within each performance, generally four strike-and-thrust actions with halberd and spear.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators hold that the martial dance embodies the martial image in music's six performances; within each performance there are generally four strike-and-thrust actions with halberd and spear.

sentences.zh: 戈則擊兵，矛則刺兵，玉戚非可施於擊刺，今舞執幹戚，蓋沿襲之誤。

translations.literal: The halberd is the striking weapon, the spear is the thrusting weapon; the jade axe cannot be applied to striking and thrusting—today's dance holding shield and axe is likely an error handed down through imitation.
translations.idiomatic: The halberd is the striking weapon, the spear the thrusting weapon; the jade axe cannot be used for striking and thrusting—today's dancers holding shield and axe is likely an error inherited through long imitation.

sentences.zh: 請左執幹，右執戈。

translations.literal: We ask: left hand hold shield, right hand hold halberd.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the left hand hold the shield and the right hand the halberd.

sentences.zh: 其五、古之鄉射禮，三笙一和而成聲，謂三人吹笙，一人吹和。

translations.literal: Fifth: in antiquity's village archery rite, three sheng and one he-harmony complete the sound—meaning three people blow sheng, one person blows the harmony pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: in the ancient village archery rite, three sheng and one harmony pipe complete the sound—three players on sheng and one on the harmony pipe.

sentences.zh: 今朝會作樂，丹墀之上，巢笙、和笙各二人，其數相敵，非也。

translations.literal: In today's court assembly music, on the red steps, nest-sheng and harmony-sheng two people each—the numbers equal each other; this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In today's court assembly music, on the red steps there are two nest-sheng players and two harmony-sheng players—the numbers are equal, and this is wrong.

sentences.zh: 蓋鄉射乃列國大夫、士之禮，請增倍為八人，丹墀東西各三巢一和。

translations.literal: The village archery rite was the ceremony of feudal states' grandees and gentlemen; we ask to double to eight people—east and west of the red steps, three nest-sheng and one harmony each.
translations.idiomatic: The village archery rite was the ceremony of feudal grandees and gentlemen; we ask to double the number to eight—east and west of the red steps, three nest-sheng and one harmony pipe each.

sentences.zh: 其六、今宮縣四隅雖有建鼓、鞞、應，相傳不擊。

translations.literal: Sixth: today at the four corners of the palace ensemble there are established drums, side drums, and response drums—by tradition they are not struck.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: today at the four corners of the palace ensemble there are established drums, side drums, and response drums, but by tradition they are not struck.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，詔四建鼓並左右鞞、應合十有二，依李照所奏，以月建為均，與鎛鍾相應。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era, an edict prescribed four established drums plus left and right bi and ying totaling twelve, following Li Zhao's memorial, using the monthly establishment as the standard tone, responding to the suspended bells.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiande era, an edict prescribed four established drums plus left and right side and response drums, twelve in all, following Li Zhao's memorial, using the monthly establishment as the standard tone to match the suspended bells.

sentences.zh: 鞞、應在建鼓旁，是亦朔鼙、應鼙之類。

translations.literal: The bi and ying stand beside the established drums—they are also of the kind of new-moon drums and response drums.
translations.idiomatic: The side and response drums stand beside the established drums—they belong to the same class as new-moon drums and response drums.

sentences.zh: 請將作樂之時，先擊鼙，次擊應，然後擊建鼓。

translations.literal: We ask that when music is about to be performed, strike the military drum first, then the response drum, then the established drum.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that when music is about to be performed, the military drum be struck first, then the response drum, and then the established drum.

sentences.zh: 其七、今樂縣四隅設建鼓，不擊，別施散鼓於樂縣內代之。

translations.literal: Seventh: today at the four corners of the music ensemble established drums are set but not struck; separate loose drums are placed within the music ensemble instead.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: today established drums are set at the four corners of the music ensemble but not struck; loose drums are placed within the ensemble instead.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，尹拙奏宜去散鼓，詔可，而樂工積習亦不能廢。

translations.literal: In Qiande, Yin Zhuo memorialized that the loose drums should be removed; the edict approved, yet the music workers' long-established practice could not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande, Yin Zhuo memorialized that the loose drums should be removed; the edict approved, yet the musicians' long-established practice could not be set aside.

sentences.zh: 李照議作晉鼓，以為樂節。

translations.literal: Li Zhao proposed making Jin drums to serve as music beat markers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao proposed making Jin drums to serve as beat markers for the music.

sentences.zh: 請樂縣內去散鼓，設晉鼓以鼓金奏。

translations.literal: We ask to remove loose drums from within the music ensemble and set up Jin drums to beat the metal performance.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to remove the loose drums from within the music ensemble and set up Jin drums to beat the metal performance.

sentences.zh: 其八、古者，瞽蒙、氐瞭皆掌播鞀，所以節一唱之終。

translations.literal: Eighth: in antiquity, blind musicians and sighted attendants all managed sounding the handheld drum, thereby marking the end of one phrase of song.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: in antiquity blind musicians and their sighted attendants all managed the handheld drum, marking the end of each phrase of song.

sentences.zh: 請宮縣設鞀，以為樂節。

translations.literal: We ask to set up handheld drums in the palace ensemble to serve as music beat markers.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that handheld drums be set up in the palace ensemble to serve as beat markers.

sentences.zh: 其九、以天子禮求之，凡樂事播鞀，擊頌磬、笙磬，以鍾鼓奏《九夏》，是皆在庭之樂；

translations.literal: Ninth: seeking by the Son of Heaven's rites, for all music affairs: sounding the handheld drum, striking the ode chime-stones and sheng chime-stones, performing the "Nine Summers" with bells and drums—these are all music in the courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: judged by the Son of Heaven's rites, all music affairs—sounding the handheld drum, striking the ode and sheng chime-stones, performing the "Nine Summers" with bells and drums—belong to the music of the courtyard;

sentences.zh: 戛擊則敔，球則玉磬，搏拊所以節樂，琴瑟所以詠詩，皆堂上樂也。

translations.literal: Striking with the scraper is the wooden tiger-rattle; the sphere is the jade chime-stone; the clapping frames mark the music beat; zither and lute recite the ode—all are hall music.
translations.idiomatic: The scraper-strike is the wooden tiger-rattle; the sphere is the jade chime-stone; the clapping frames mark the beat; zither and lute recite the ode—all are hall music.

sentences.zh: 磬本在堂下，尊玉磬，故進之使在上，若擊石拊石，則當在庭。

translations.literal: Chime-stones originally stood below the hall; honoring the jade chime-stones, they were advanced to stand above—if striking stone and clapping stone, that belongs in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Chime-stones originally stood below the hall; to honor the jade chime-stones, they were moved above—whereas striking stone and clapping stone belongs in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 後世不原於此，以春秋鄭人賂晉俟歌鍾二肆，遂於堂上設歌鍾、歌磬，蓋歌鍾則堂上歌之，堂下以鼓應之耳。

translations.literal: Later ages did not trace this to its source; because in the Spring and Autumn Annals the people of Zheng bribed the Jin marquis with two sets of song-bells, thereafter song-bells and song chime-stones were set up in the hall—presumably for song-bells, one sings above the hall while below the hall drums respond—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages did not trace this to its source; because in the Spring and Autumn Annals the people of Zheng bribed the Jin marquis with two sets of song-bells, song-bells and song chime-stones were thereafter set up in the hall—yet for song-bells, one sings above the hall while drums below respond; that is all.

sentences.zh: 歌必金奏相和，名曰歌鍾，則以節歌是已，豈堂上有鍾邪？

translations.literal: Song must have metal performance harmonizing with it—called song-bells—it is merely to mark the song; how could there be bells above the hall?
translations.idiomatic: Song requires metal performance to harmonize with it—the so-called song-bells merely mark the song; how could there be bells above the hall?

sentences.zh: 歌磬之名，本無所出，晉賀循奏置登歌簨虡，采玉造小磬，蓋取舜廟鳴球之製。

translations.literal: The name "song chime-stones" originally has no source; Jin's He Xun memorialized to set up ascent-singing frames, gathering jade to make small chime-stones—probably taking the design from Shun's voice of the suspended sphere in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The name "song chime-stones" has no genuine origin; Jin's He Xun memorialized to set up ascent-singing frames and gather jade to make small chime-stones, probably taking the design from the sounding sphere in Shun's temple.

sentences.zh: 後周登歌，備錄鍾磬，隋、唐迄今，因襲行之，皆不應禮。

translations.literal: The Later Zhou's ascent singing fully included bells and chime-stones; from Sui and Tang to the present, inherited and carried out—all failing to accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Zhou's ascent singing fully included bells and chime-stones; from Sui and Tang to the present this has been inherited and carried out—all contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 請正、至朝會，堂上之樂不設鍾磬。

translations.literal: We ask that at New Year's and winter solstice court assemblies, hall music not include bells and chime-stones.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that at New Year's and winter solstice court assemblies, bells and chime-stones not be set up among the hall music.

sentences.zh: 其十、古者歌工之數：大射工六人，四瑟，則是諸侯鼓瑟以四人，歌以二人；

translations.literal: Tenth: in antiquity the number of song workers—at the great archery rite six workers, four se lutes—meaning feudal lords play se with four people, sing with two;
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: in antiquity the number of song workers—at the great archery rite six workers and four se lutes—meaning feudal lords had four se players and two singers;

sentences.zh: 天子八人，則瑟與歌皆四人矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven eight people—then se and song are four each.
translations.idiomatic: For the Son of Heaven, eight workers—then se and song were four each.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，登歌五人，隋、唐四人，本朝因之，是循用周製也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, ascent singing five people; Sui and Tang four people; our dynasty follows this—it is following the Zhou system.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward ascent singing had five performers, Sui and Tang four, and our dynasty follows this—claiming to follow the Zhou system.

sentences.zh: 《禮》“登歌下管”，貴人聲也，故《儀禮》瑟與歌工皆席於西階上。

translations.literal: The Rites: "ascent singing, descent pipes"—honoring human voice; therefore in the Ceremonies and Rites, se and song workers all sit on the western steps above.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say "ascent singing, descent pipes," honoring the human voice; therefore in the Ceremonies and Rites, se and song workers all sit on the western steps above.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐相承，庭中磬虡之下，係以偶歌琴瑟，非所謂升歌貴人聲之義。

translations.literal: Sui and Tang inherited each other—below the chime frames in the courtyard, paired song with zither and se attached—not the meaning of ascent singing honoring human voice.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Tang inherited this practice—below the chime frames in the courtyard, paired singing with zither and se was attached—not the meaning of ascent singing honoring the human voice.

sentences.zh: 今堂上琴瑟，比之周製，不啻倍蓰，而歌工止四人，音高下不相權。

translations.literal: Today hall zithers and se, compared with the Zhou system, are not merely doubled or multiplied; yet song workers only four—the high and low tones do not balance each other.
translations.idiomatic: Today the hall zithers and se, compared with the Zhou system, are more than doubled, yet song workers number only four—the high and low tones do not balance.

sentences.zh: 蓋樂有八音，所以行八風，是以舞佾與鍾磬俱用八為數。

translations.literal: Music has eight tones, thereby carrying the eight winds—therefore dance rows and bells and chime-stones all use eight as their number.
translations.idiomatic: Music has eight tones to carry the eight winds—therefore dance rows, bells, and chime-stones all use eight as their number.

sentences.zh: 請罷庭中歌者，堂上歌為八，琴瑟之數放此，其箏、阮、築悉廢。

translations.literal: We ask to abolish singers in the courtyard; hall singers become eight, zither and se numbers follow this pattern; zheng, ruan, and zhu instruments all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to abolish singers in the courtyard, set hall singers at eight, match the number of zithers and se to this, and abolish the zheng, ruan, and zhu entirely.

sentences.zh: 太常以謂：“堂上鍾磬去之，則歌聲與宮縣遠。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices said: "If bells and chime-stones above the hall are removed, then the singing voice is far from the palace ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices said: "If bells and chime-stones above the hall are removed, the singing voice will be far from the palace ensemble.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐以來，宮室之製浸廣，堂上益遠庭中，其上下樂節苟不相應，則繁亂而無序。

translations.literal: From Han and Tang onward, palace halls have gradually expanded; the hall is ever farther from the courtyard—if the music beats above and below do not correspond, then chaos and disorder without sequence.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Tang onward palace halls have gradually expanded, and the hall grows ever farther from the courtyard; if the beats above and below do not correspond, the result is chaos and disorder.

sentences.zh: 況朝會之禮，起於西漢，則後世難以純用三代之製。

translations.literal: Moreover court assembly rites originated in the Western Han—then later ages can hardly purely use the Three Dynasties' system.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover court assembly rites originated in the Western Han, so later ages can hardly adopt the Three Dynasties' system in pure form.

sentences.zh: 其堂上鍾磬、庭中歌工與箏、築之器，從舊儀便。”

translations.literal: As for hall bells and chime-stones, courtyard song workers, and zheng and zhu instruments—follow the old rites for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: As for hall bells and chime-stones, courtyard song workers, and zheng and zhu instruments, let the old rites stand for convenience."

sentences.zh: 遂如太常議。

translations.literal: It was done as the Director of Imperial Sacrifices proposed.
translations.idiomatic: It was done as the Director of Imperial Sacrifices proposed.
